1	---
2	epic: 8
3	date: 2026-11-08
4	verdict: accepted-with-open-items
5	criteria: profiled
6	headless: false
7	---
8	
9	# Epic 8 Retrospective — Evolution Dashboard & Account Management
10	
11	## Epic summary
12	
13	Epic 8 is the **final functional-requirement unit** in the project's delivery order (`docs/input/requirements.md` §12: `F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09`, with RF09 = account deletion, last). It shipped five stories, each its own commit:
14	
15	| Story | Commit | Summary |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| 8.1 | `6548fec` | On-demand dashboard aggregation (0/1/>30-entry chart states) |
18	| 8.2 | `dd59fc8` | Independent narrative text + narrative-unavailable state |
19	| 8.3 | `150b89d` | Inline profile name editing |
20	| 8.4 | `45b2dcd` | Logout |
21	| 8.5 | `c4c355d` | Account deletion |
22	| — | `71b5bdc` | "RF09: closing snapshot at unit completion" — closes a deferred e2e-coverage gap for `deleteAccount()`, reconciles `tests/test-summary.md` |
23	
24	**Diff range:** `6548fec^..71b5bdc` (the `^` includes 8.1's own commit; the closing-snapshot commit is included because it touches real `lib/`/`test/` code for this epic's account feature, not just docs). `git_evidence.py` over this range: 6 non-merge commits, 0 merges, 84 files touched. Automatic per-commit story attribution (`git_evidence.py --stories`) returned empty for every commit — commit subjects say "story 8.1" etc., not the `8-1-...` id format the script word-matches — so story-to-commit mapping above was done by hand from `git log` and is unambiguous (one story per commit, strictly sequential).
25	
26	**Sprint status:** all 5 stories `done`, no `pending_stories` for epic 8 (confirmed via `sprint_status.py detect-epic`). User confirmed epic 8 as the retro target interactively before Phase 1 began.
27	
28	**Evidence available:** epic spec (`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md` §"Epic 8"), epic context (`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-8-context.md`), all 5 story specs with full "Review Findings"/"Spec Change Log"/"Verification" sections, `deferred-work.md`'s per-story deferred entries, `tests/test-summary.md`'s final ledger, current repo state (re-ran `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` directly rather than trusting the ledger).
29	
30	**Evidence missing:** no session logs exist for this epic's implementation (only planning-stage `.memlog.md` files exist, none for dev work) — process-lesson analysis below is sourced from the story specs' own self-recorded review findings and spec-change-logs, not from a session transcript. No previous retrospective exists for any earlier epic (1–7 retro keys are all still `optional`, never run) — see Previous-retro follow-through.
31	
32	## Findings
33	
34	Each finding's disposition (fix now / defer / accept-as-is) is in Action items / Open items below. Findings already known and recorded in `deferred-work.md` during the epic's own story-level reviews are listed under "Already known" and are **not** re-routed.
35	
36	### New — seam findings (visible only once all 5 stories' code coexists)
37	
38	Produced by three parallel review-lens passes (adversarial, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) over the final merged state of `account_settings_cubit.dart`, `account_settings_screen.dart`, `account_settings_repository_impl.dart`, `dashboard_cubit.dart`, `dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart`, `dashboard_chart_section.dart`, cross-checked against the 6-commit diff. Each item below was independently spot-verified against the source file before being kept (per-item note says what was checked).
39	
40	1. **Narrative-error announce listener bypasses the dedup guard its sibling listener was given.** `account_settings_screen.dart`'s `BlocListener<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>` (narrative-triggered, added by spec-8-2's amendment) announces "narrativa indisponível" on every `ResourceError` emission with no dedup check. Its sibling `BlocListener<DashboardCubit, ...>` (dashboard-triggered, added one story later by a spec-8-4 review patch) was given a `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` flag specifically to stop repeat announcements of the same unresolved error — but that flag is written only by the second listener; the first bypasses it entirely. *Verified*: read both listener bodies directly (lines ~525–602); confirmed the narrative-triggered listener has no reference to `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced`. *Consequence*: tapping "tentar novamente" repeatedly while the narrative keeps failing re-triggers a VoiceOver announcement on every tap — the exact spam the sibling fix exists to prevent, reachable through the other listener. — **adversarial lens**
41	
42	2. **`clearStaleError()` never clears `deleteAccountErrorMessage`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:278-282`'s `clearStaleError()` — written in spec-8-1/8.3 specifically so a DI-singleton cubit's leftover error text doesn't linger into an unrelated later screen visit — only clears the biometric-toggle `errorMessage` field. `deleteAccountErrorMessage` was added two stories later (8.5) and never got the same treatment; `initState()`'s single call site (`screen.dart:93`) only reaches the older field. *Verified*: read `clearStaleError()`'s body and its one call site; confirmed it checks only `state.errorMessage`. *Consequence*: after a failed "Apagar conta" attempt, leaving Configurações via the back arrow and returning later (no new attempt) still shows the stale deletion-failure message — the exact bug `clearStaleError()` was built to prevent, reproduced for the field added after it. — **independently found by both the adversarial and edge-case-hunter lenses**
43	
44	3. **`deleteAccount()` is the only write method in `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl` with no generation guard.** `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName` each capture `++_generation`/`++_nameGeneration` and discard a superseded result; `deleteAccount()` (`account_settings_repository_impl.dart:212-213`) is a bare pass-through with no counter at all, despite the class's own doc comment stating "every call captures the generation current at its own start" as its concurrency convention. *Verified*: `grep -n "_generation\|deleteAccount"` on the file — confirmed no counter touches the `deleteAccount` line. *Consequence*: the one new repository method this epic added quietly breaks the class's own stated invariant; a future reader who trusts "every write here is generation-guarded" is wrong specifically for the operation where getting concurrency handling wrong matters most. — **adversarial lens**
45	
46	4. **`deleteAccount()` cubit method has `try`/`finally` with no `catch`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:465-481`: if `_repository.deleteAccount()` or `_finishSession()` throws instead of resolving to `Either` (nothing currently does, but nothing enforces that — the same caveat `logout()`'s own `try`/`finally` patch already documents for itself), the exception propagates uncaught; `isDeletingAccount` resets via `finally`, but no error is ever shown. *Verified*: read the method body directly — confirmed no `catch` clause exists. — **edge-case-hunter lens**
47	
48	5. **Dashboard aggregate's error card has no retry link; the narrative's does.** `dashboard_chart_section.dart`'s `_errorCard` (story 8.1) renders static text only; `_narrativeSection`'s `ResourceError` branch (story 8.2, same file) explicitly added a "tentar novamente" retry link for a failure of the identical shape. *Verified*: grepped both branches — confirmed no `GestureDetector`/`onTap` in `_errorCard`. *Consequence*: a user whose main chart fails to load has no in-screen recovery path, while the narrative directly below it does, for the same failure class. — **adversarial lens**
49	
50	6. **"Apagar conta" shipped with the same missing-loading-indicator gap "Sair" already had — and didn't log the recurrence.** Spec-8-4's own review found and *explicitly deferred* "Sair" having no loading indicator while `isLoggingOut`. Spec-8-5 then added "Apagar conta" with the identical `onPressed: null`-only pattern and no indicator, and its own Review Findings section never mentions it. *Verified*: read both buttons (`screen.dart` ~614–667) — neither has a `CircularProgressIndicator`; `deferred-work.md`'s spec-8-5 entries contain no matching item. *Disposition*: the underlying gap is the same already-accepted tradeoff (shared `AppButton` primitive has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify a layout change) — **accept as-is**, same rationale as "Sair"'s own deferral. The actionable lesson is process, not code: a later story reusing a pattern a prior story already deferred should cross-reference the existing deferral instead of leaving a second, unlinked instance of the same gap. — **adversarial lens**
51	
52	7. **`_emptyCard`'s padding wasn't updated by the round-2 "no card-resize" fix that touched its siblings.** Story 8.1's round-2 review fix switched `_loadingCard`/`_errorCard`/`_populatedCard` to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding` (20) specifically so the card wouldn't visibly resize across a loading→data transition — `_emptyCard` (the zero-entries state) was left on `DesignTokens.spacingLg` (24). *Verified*: `grep -n "dashboardCardPadding\|spacingLg"` on the file — confirmed `_emptyCard` at line 113 is the only card-builder still using `spacingLg`. *Consequence*: a first-time user with zero entries sees exactly the card-resize jump the fix was written to eliminate everywhere else. — **adversarial lens**
53	
54	8. **Biometric-toggle and name-save spinners have no `semanticsLabel`; the dashboard's identical spinner does.** Story 8.1 gave the dashboard's `CircularProgressIndicator` an explicit `semanticsLabel` ("Carregando gráfico de evolução") as a dedicated accessibility fix. The two near-identical spinners already on the same merged screen (biometric `isSaving`, name-edit `isSavingName`) have none. *Consequence*: a VoiceOver user saving a name or toggling biometric login gets no spoken in-progress feedback, unlike the dashboard's own loading state on the same screen. — **adversarial lens**
55	
56	9. **Narrative `ResourceData` with a blank/whitespace-only string is an unhandled implicit third state.** The render path (`dashboard_chart_section.dart`) already trims and suppresses a blank narrative string (a dedicated round-2 test covers this); but the two announce-listeners in `account_settings_screen.dart` only check `is ResourceError<String>` — a successful-but-blank response neither renders nor announces, silently falling through both paths. *Verified*: re-read both listener bodies; neither inspects `ResourceData.data` for blankness. Low severity (no crash, no visible defect — the card already handles this correctly), but a genuinely unhandled implicit branch. — **edge-case-hunter lens**
57	
58	10. **`AccountSettingsCubit`'s one-time construction-time read of `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail` depends on an unenforced boot-ordering assumption.** The cubit reads these fields exactly once, at DI-singleton construction; correctness depends on `main()`'s boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` call having already resolved by the time something first resolves `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()` — nothing asserts or enforces that ordering. *Disposition*: architectural risk, not a current bug (today's DI wiring satisfies the ordering) — **defer**, revisit if DI bootstrap ever changes (eager registration, splash prefetch, new test harness). — **adversarial lens**
59	
60	11. **A failed boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` leaves the name/email header permanently blank for the session.** `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` are populated only by piggybacking on a successful boot fetch or a successful `setDisplayName()` call; nothing retries if both of `main.dart`'s one-shot boot attempts fail (e.g., app opened offline). *Disposition*: real but narrow (requires offline app launch) — **defer**, propose retrying the fetch the next time Configurações opens rather than relying solely on the two boot-time attempts. — **adversarial lens**
61	
62	### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed)
63	
64	Confirmed still present in the current code; logged in `deferred-work.md` under the relevant `spec-8-*` headings. Listed here only because the verification-gap lens independently re-derived the first one with corroborating detail:
65	
66	- **`clearLocalCache()` not coordinated with in-flight writes/fetches** (`deferred-work.md`, spec-8-4 entry) — the verification-gap lens independently re-confirmed this for `EntriesRepository` (an in-flight `create()`/`retry()` can repopulate the just-cleared box) *and* additionally traced the same shape through `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` (an in-flight fetch, not just a write, can repopulate the just-cleared chat boxes) — broadening, not replacing, the existing entry. **Action item 12** below proposes folding this broader evidence into the existing `deferred-work.md` entry.
67	- The shared `_finishSession()` re-entry race (logout/deleteAccount/toggleBiometric/confirmEditingName can race each other).
68	- In-memory singleton state (cached name/email, dashboard aggregate, chat session, pending-write tracker) not reset on logout/delete.
69	- `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit`'s `confirmedWrites` subscriptions living for the whole app session, not just while mounted.
70	- Vault PIN never cleared on logout (explicitly flagged as ambiguous, not a defect).
71	- `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` using `Failure.malformedResponse` for local-storage faults (pre-existing codebase convention).
72	- No real-DI e2e test for `deleteAccount()`'s full orchestration at the time of spec-8-5's own review — **closed** by the `71b5bdc` closing-snapshot commit, which added exactly this.
73	- `SessionRepositoryImpl.logout()`'s silent `catch (_) {}` (deliberately mirrors an existing same-file convention).
74	- The narrative fetch firing unconditionally regardless of entry count (one harmless extra backend call for 0/1-count users) — explicitly accepted in spec-8-2's own Design Notes as the cost of keeping the two `Resource`s genuinely decoupled.
75	
76	### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)
77	
78	- **Architecture / layering — clean.** `grep`-verified: no domain-layer file in `dashboard/` or `account/` imports `package:flutter` or anything from a `data/` layer. All new repository methods return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09). `AccountSettingsCubit` depends only on domain-layer repository interfaces (`SessionRepository`, `VaultRepository`, `EntriesRepository`, `ChatRepository`, `AccountSettingsRepository`) — no cross-feature data-layer imports (RNF06). All five backend calls (`dashboard-aggregate-get`, `dashboard-narrative-get`, `account-settings-update`, `account-delete`, `auth-logout`) match `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping exactly, called by name per AGENTS.md's convention. Zero hardcoded visual values introduced (`grep` for `Color(0x`/raw px literals in the epic's new widget files found none).
79	- **God-class / size growth.** `account_settings_screen.dart` grew to 677 lines across all 6 commits in this range (net +538 lines over the epic) with a single `build()` method spanning ~354 lines (biometric toggle + dashboard chart + narrative + profile header + name-edit + logout + delete-account, all inline, each story adding its own section without extraction). `account_settings_cubit.dart` grew to 489 lines (net +343) and now owns four largely-unrelated concerns (biometric toggle, name editing, logout, account deletion) in one class. Each story's own in-diff review correctly judged its *own* increment as reasonable; nothing in the per-story process was positioned to notice the cumulative size. The per-line code quality is good — guards, tests, and provenance comments are consistent throughout, confirmed by direct reading — this is a structural/SRP observation, not a correctness defect. **Disposition: accept as-is for this delivery** (no functional requirement calls for splitting it, and extraction now is a refactor with regression risk, not a bug fix); **propose as a follow-up** if this screen gains a 6th concern.
80	- **Duplication — deliberate, self-documented, by design.** `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit` are near-total structural duplicates (`diff` of the two files shows only the obvious renames/type changes) — but each file's own doc comment explicitly cross-references the other and states the mirroring is intentional per frozen Boundaries text ("mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape"). **Accept as-is** — this is accepted deviation, not an accidental reimplementation from one session not knowing the other existed. The one real cost of the duplication (the identical untested `onError`-handler gap existing in both files) is already tracked in `deferred-work.md`.
81	- **Spec-to-implementation reconciliation — two real spec bugs caught and fixed, both properly reconciled.** Story 8.1's frozen `>30`-entry condensation algorithm degenerated for `bucketCounts.length < 10` (9 invisible bars + 1 giant bar) — found by review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` (root cause sat inside `<frozen-after-approval>` text), fixed with an explicit Spec Change Log entry (left-pad amendment) per direct human instruction to use technical judgment over the heavier revert-and-replan protocol. Story 8.2's frozen narrative-announcement line was unconditional, in tension with the adjacent "never show narrative for 0/1-count" line — same catch-and-reconcile pattern, same human-routed resolution. Both are exactly the "spec that should be reconciled to reality" case this retro's own catalog describes, and both were *already* reconciled in-story with full evidence trails — no outstanding reconciliation work remains from either.
82	
83	## Behavior verification
84	
85	No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists for this project (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope, consistent with every story's own Verification section. What was actually exercised in this retro, directly, not from the record alone:
86	
87	- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
88	- `fvm flutter test` (full suite) — re-ran: **1309/1309 passing**, exactly matching `tests/test-summary.md`'s own final ledger (no drift found this time, unlike the 3 earlier drifts the epic's own stories caught and corrected in-flight).
89	- The project's real-DI e2e suite (`test/features/account/account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart`, `test/features/dashboard/dashboard_flow_e2e_test.dart`) — the closest thing to an end-to-end behavior check this repo has — exercises the genuine DI graph (`sl<...>()`) with fakes only at the HTTP transport boundary, covering logout, account deletion (happy path, backend failure, double-tap no-op), and dashboard aggregate/narrative fetch+recompute, confirmed read directly as part of the review above.
90	
91	No manual/visual walkthrough was performed (no device/simulator exists) — this is an explicit scope gap, not "checked and clean," same as every story's own Verification section already states.
92	
93	## Previous-retro follow-through
94	
95	No previous retrospective exists for any earlier epic — `sprint-status.yaml` shows `epic-1-retrospective` through `epic-7-retrospective` all still `optional`, none ever run, and there are no `action_items` in the file at all. Nothing to follow through on.
96	
97	## Action items
98	
99	Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro; the next dev session executes and verifies against the normal `fvm flutter analyze`/`fvm flutter test` gate):
100	
101	1. **Fix the narrative-error announce dedup bypass** — route the narrative-triggered `BlocListener` (finding 1) through the same `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` state the dashboard-triggered listener already uses, so neither path can re-announce an already-announced, still-failing narrative error. *Owner: dev, next pass on `account_settings_screen.dart`.*
102	2. **Widen `clearStaleError()` to also clear `deleteAccountErrorMessage`** (finding 2), or add a sibling clear call from `initState()`. *Owner: dev.*
103	3. **Give `deleteAccount()` its own generation guard** (finding 3), consistent with `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName`. *Owner: dev.*
104	4. **Add a `catch` to `deleteAccount()`'s cubit method** (finding 4) so an unexpected throw surfaces an error instead of silently resetting state. *Owner: dev.*
105	5. **Add a retry affordance to the dashboard aggregate's `_errorCard`** (finding 5), matching the narrative section's existing "tentar novamente" link. *Owner: dev.*
106	6. **Fix `_emptyCard`'s padding** (finding 7) to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding`, matching its sibling cards. *Owner: dev — trivial, one-line.*
107	7. **Add `semanticsLabel` to the biometric-toggle and name-save spinners** (finding 8), matching the dashboard chart's existing accessibility treatment. *Owner: dev.*
108	
109	Deferred items (tracked, not blocking, context attached so a later pass doesn't need to re-investigate):
110	
111	8. Finding 6 ("Apagar conta" missing-loading-indicator recurrence) — **accept as-is**, same rationale already on record for "Sair"; cross-reference the two `deferred-work.md`-worthy notes if either is ever revisited.
112	9. Finding 9 (blank/whitespace narrative success falls through both render and announce paths) — low severity; propose treating a blank `ResourceData` the same as the narrative-unavailable case if ever touched again.
113	10. Finding 10 (unenforced boot-ordering assumption behind `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail`'s one-time read) — revisit only if DI bootstrap ordering changes.
114	11. Finding 11 (no retry for a failed boot-time name/email fetch) — revisit if offline-launch UX becomes a priority.
115	12. **Broaden `deferred-work.md`'s existing spec-8-4 `clearLocalCache()`-race entry** to explicitly name `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` repopulation alongside the already-named `create()`/`sendMessage()`/`retryMessage()` — the verification-gap lens traced the fetch-side (not just write-side) manifestation with concrete evidence this retro's Findings section records. *Owner: dev — documentation-only update to the existing ledger entry, not new code.*
116	
117	Process lessons (what would prevent the next one — no action required unless a future epic recurs):
118	
119	- **A later story adding a second guard/listener for a concern a prior story already partially solved should diff against the sibling, not just review its own new code.** Findings 1 and 8 are both this shape: a later story's accessibility/dedup fix was added without checking whether an earlier story's own near-identical control already needed, or already had, the same treatment. The per-story 4-layer review process is excellent at catching defects in a story's own diff; it has no step that asks "does a sibling control on this same merged screen already have this, or need this too?" — worth adding as an explicit check the next time a story extends an existing shared screen/cubit rather than building a new one.
120	- **A story that re-ships an already-deferred gap under a different name should log the recurrence, not leave it silent.** Finding 6 (spec-8-5 reproducing spec-8-4's own already-deferred "no loading indicator" gap without mentioning it) is low-impact here because the underlying disposition is correctly "accept as-is" either way — but the pattern is worth naming: a recurrence of a *known* gap is cheap to flag with one cross-referencing sentence and easy to miss silently once code review assumes "this is new, not a repeat."
121	- **Worth keeping, not fixing**: the human-routed spec-amendment path (Spec Change Log entries for stories 8.1 and 8.2) worked exactly as intended — two genuinely wrong pieces of *frozen, previously-approved* spec text were caught by post-implementation review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently patched or silently left broken, and resolved with an explicit, evidenced amendment plus a "KEEP" list protecting everything that was already correct. This is the retrospective's own job (catching what no single session could see) already happening *inside* the epic, one story at a time — the fact that two such catches were needed in one five-story epic is itself worth noting for anyone estimating how often frozen spec text needs this safety valve.
122	
123	## Acceptance verdict
124	
125	**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria profiled, not declared — epic 8 has no dedicated acceptance-criteria document beyond `epics.md`'s own per-story Given/When/Then text, which this retro treated as the criteria to profile against).
126	
127	Evidence for "criteria met":
128	- All three dashboard entry-count states (0/1/>30) implemented, tested, and the one algorithmic defect in the >30 condensation found and fixed in-story with an evidenced spec amendment.
129	- Narrative text ships as a genuinely independent fetch (never coupled to the chart `Resource`), with a distinct narrative-unavailable state — confirmed by direct code read, not just the spec's own claim.
130	- Inline name editing matches every I/O-matrix row (pencil→check, save, tap-away revert, failure-keeps-draft) with dedicated widget tests for each.
131	- Logout calls `auth-logout`, routes to the vault/login screen, and clears both the entries and chat Hive caches (closing the pre-existing shared-device data-leak gap this epic's own spec named as a goal).
132	- Account deletion uses the destructive-variant red-title dialog, hard-deletes via `DELETE /account`, routes to the same destination as logout, and traps focus while the dialog is open — all confirmed present in code.
133	- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test`: 1309/1309 passing, re-verified directly in this retro.
134	- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, RNF09, or design-token violations found anywhere in the epic's diff.
135	
136	Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 11 new findings (1 real correctness bug surfaced to users — the announce-dedup bypass, finding 1 — the rest are consistency/accessibility/architectural-risk items of lesser severity), none of which represent a failure to deliver the epic's own stated functionality. No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty). No finding rises to "criteria not met."
137	
138	## Open questions
139	
140	- Should the already-accepted "no loading indicator on Sair/Apagar conta" gap (findings/deferred item 6, 8) be revisited now that it has recurred twice in the same epic, or does the existing rationale (shared `AppButton` has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify) still hold? This is a product/design call, not something this retro can resolve on its own.
141	- Is the offline-boot name/email-blank gap (deferred item 11) worth a fix now, or is it acceptable given the app's general assumption of connectivity at launch? No `docs/input/` text addresses offline-launch UX directly.

# Epic 8 Retrospective — Evolution Dashboard & Account Management

## Epic summary

Epic 8 is the **final functional-requirement unit** in the project's delivery order (`docs/input/requirements.md` §12: `F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09`, with RF09 = account deletion, last). It shipped five stories, each its own commit:

| Story | Commit | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 8.1 | `6548fec` | On-demand dashboard aggregation (0/1/>30-entry chart states) |
| 8.2 | `dd59fc8` | Independent narrative text + narrative-unavailable state |
| 8.3 | `150b89d` | Inline profile name editing |
| 8.4 | `45b2dcd` | Logout |
| 8.5 | `c4c355d` | Account deletion |
| — | `71b5bdc` | "RF09: closing snapshot at unit completion" — closes a deferred e2e-coverage gap for `deleteAccount()`, reconciles `tests/test-summary.md` |

**Diff range:** `6548fec^..71b5bdc` (the `^` includes 8.1's own commit; the closing-snapshot commit is included because it touches real `lib/`/`test/` code for this epic's account feature, not just docs). `git_evidence.py` over this range: 6 non-merge commits, 0 merges, 84 files touched. Automatic per-commit story attribution (`git_evidence.py --stories`) returned empty for every commit — commit subjects say "story 8.1" etc., not the `8-1-...` id format the script word-matches — so story-to-commit mapping above was done by hand from `git log` and is unambiguous (one story per commit, strictly sequential).

**Sprint status:** all 5 stories `done`, no `pending_stories` for epic 8 (confirmed via `sprint_status.py detect-epic`). User confirmed epic 8 as the retro target interactively before Phase 1 began.

**Evidence available:** epic spec (`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md` §"Epic 8"), epic context (`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-8-context.md`), all 5 story specs with full "Review Findings"/"Spec Change Log"/"Verification" sections, `deferred-work.md`'s per-story deferred entries, `tests/test-summary.md`'s final ledger, current repo state (re-ran `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` directly rather than trusting the ledger).

**Evidence missing:** no session logs exist for this epic's implementation (only planning-stage `.memlog.md` files exist, none for dev work) — process-lesson analysis below is sourced from the story specs' own self-recorded review findings and spec-change-logs, not from a session transcript. No previous retrospective exists for any earlier epic (1–7 retro keys are all still `optional`, never run) — see Previous-retro follow-through.

## Findings

Each finding's disposition (fix now / defer / accept-as-is) is in Action items / Open items below. Findings already known and recorded in `deferred-work.md` during the epic's own story-level reviews are listed under "Already known" and are **not** re-routed.

### New — seam findings (visible only once all 5 stories' code coexists)

Produced by three parallel review-lens passes (adversarial, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) over the final merged state of `account_settings_cubit.dart`, `account_settings_screen.dart`, `account_settings_repository_impl.dart`, `dashboard_cubit.dart`, `dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart`, `dashboard_chart_section.dart`, cross-checked against the 6-commit diff. Each item below was independently spot-verified against the source file before being kept (per-item note says what was checked).

1. **Narrative-error announce listener bypasses the dedup guard its sibling listener was given.** `account_settings_screen.dart`'s `BlocListener<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>` (narrative-triggered, added by spec-8-2's amendment) announces "narrativa indisponível" on every `ResourceError` emission with no dedup check. Its sibling `BlocListener<DashboardCubit, ...>` (dashboard-triggered, added one story later by a spec-8-4 review patch) was given a `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` flag specifically to stop repeat announcements of the same unresolved error — but that flag is written only by the second listener; the first bypasses it entirely. *Verified*: read both listener bodies directly (lines ~525–602); confirmed the narrative-triggered listener has no reference to `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced`. *Consequence*: tapping "tentar novamente" repeatedly while the narrative keeps failing re-triggers a VoiceOver announcement on every tap — the exact spam the sibling fix exists to prevent, reachable through the other listener. — **adversarial lens**

2. **`clearStaleError()` never clears `deleteAccountErrorMessage`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:278-282`'s `clearStaleError()` — written in spec-8-1/8.3 specifically so a DI-singleton cubit's leftover error text doesn't linger into an unrelated later screen visit — only clears the biometric-toggle `errorMessage` field. `deleteAccountErrorMessage` was added two stories later (8.5) and never got the same treatment; `initState()`'s single call site (`screen.dart:93`) only reaches the older field. *Verified*: read `clearStaleError()`'s body and its one call site; confirmed it checks only `state.errorMessage`. *Consequence*: after a failed "Apagar conta" attempt, leaving Configurações via the back arrow and returning later (no new attempt) still shows the stale deletion-failure message — the exact bug `clearStaleError()` was built to prevent, reproduced for the field added after it. — **independently found by both the adversarial and edge-case-hunter lenses**

3. **`deleteAccount()` is the only write method in `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl` with no generation guard.** `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName` each capture `++_generation`/`++_nameGeneration` and discard a superseded result; `deleteAccount()` (`account_settings_repository_impl.dart:212-213`) is a bare pass-through with no counter at all, despite the class's own doc comment stating "every call captures the generation current at its own start" as its concurrency convention. *Verified*: `grep -n "_generation\|deleteAccount"` on the file — confirmed no counter touches the `deleteAccount` line. *Consequence*: the one new repository method this epic added quietly breaks the class's own stated invariant; a future reader who trusts "every write here is generation-guarded" is wrong specifically for the operation where getting concurrency handling wrong matters most. — **adversarial lens**

4. **`deleteAccount()` cubit method has `try`/`finally` with no `catch`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:465-481`: if `_repository.deleteAccount()` or `_finishSession()` throws instead of resolving to `Either` (nothing currently does, but nothing enforces that — the same caveat `logout()`'s own `try`/`finally` patch already documents for itself), the exception propagates uncaught; `isDeletingAccount` resets via `finally`, but no error is ever shown. *Verified*: read the method body directly — confirmed no `catch` clause exists. — **edge-case-hunter lens**

5. **Dashboard aggregate's error card has no retry link; the narrative's does.** `dashboard_chart_section.dart`'s `_errorCard` (story 8.1) renders static text only; `_narrativeSection`'s `ResourceError` branch (story 8.2, same file) explicitly added a "tentar novamente" retry link for a failure of the identical shape. *Verified*: grepped both branches — confirmed no `GestureDetector`/`onTap` in `_errorCard`. *Consequence*: a user whose main chart fails to load has no in-screen recovery path, while the narrative directly below it does, for the same failure class. — **adversarial lens**

6. **"Apagar conta" shipped with the same missing-loading-indicator gap "Sair" already had — and didn't log the recurrence.** Spec-8-4's own review found and *explicitly deferred* "Sair" having no loading indicator while `isLoggingOut`. Spec-8-5 then added "Apagar conta" with the identical `onPressed: null`-only pattern and no indicator, and its own Review Findings section never mentions it. *Verified*: read both buttons (`screen.dart` ~614–667) — neither has a `CircularProgressIndicator`; `deferred-work.md`'s spec-8-5 entries contain no matching item. *Disposition*: the underlying gap is the same already-accepted tradeoff (shared `AppButton` primitive has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify a layout change) — **accept as-is**, same rationale as "Sair"'s own deferral. The actionable lesson is process, not code: a later story reusing a pattern a prior story already deferred should cross-reference the existing deferral instead of leaving a second, unlinked instance of the same gap. — **adversarial lens**

7. **`_emptyCard`'s padding wasn't updated by the round-2 "no card-resize" fix that touched its siblings.** Story 8.1's round-2 review fix switched `_loadingCard`/`_errorCard`/`_populatedCard` to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding` (20) specifically so the card wouldn't visibly resize across a loading→data transition — `_emptyCard` (the zero-entries state) was left on `DesignTokens.spacingLg` (24). *Verified*: `grep -n "dashboardCardPadding\|spacingLg"` on the file — confirmed `_emptyCard` at line 113 is the only card-builder still using `spacingLg`. *Consequence*: a first-time user with zero entries sees exactly the card-resize jump the fix was written to eliminate everywhere else. — **adversarial lens**

8. **Biometric-toggle and name-save spinners have no `semanticsLabel`; the dashboard's identical spinner does.** Story 8.1 gave the dashboard's `CircularProgressIndicator` an explicit `semanticsLabel` ("Carregando gráfico de evolução") as a dedicated accessibility fix. The two near-identical spinners already on the same merged screen (biometric `isSaving`, name-edit `isSavingName`) have none. *Consequence*: a VoiceOver user saving a name or toggling biometric login gets no spoken in-progress feedback, unlike the dashboard's own loading state on the same screen. — **adversarial lens**

9. **Narrative `ResourceData` with a blank/whitespace-only string is an unhandled implicit third state.** The render path (`dashboard_chart_section.dart`) already trims and suppresses a blank narrative string (a dedicated round-2 test covers this); but the two announce-listeners in `account_settings_screen.dart` only check `is ResourceError<String>` — a successful-but-blank response neither renders nor announces, silently falling through both paths. *Verified*: re-read both listener bodies; neither inspects `ResourceData.data` for blankness. Low severity (no crash, no visible defect — the card already handles this correctly), but a genuinely unhandled implicit branch. — **edge-case-hunter lens**

10. **`AccountSettingsCubit`'s one-time construction-time read of `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail` depends on an unenforced boot-ordering assumption.** The cubit reads these fields exactly once, at DI-singleton construction; correctness depends on `main()`'s boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` call having already resolved by the time something first resolves `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()` — nothing asserts or enforces that ordering. *Disposition*: architectural risk, not a current bug (today's DI wiring satisfies the ordering) — **defer**, revisit if DI bootstrap ever changes (eager registration, splash prefetch, new test harness). — **adversarial lens**

11. **A failed boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` leaves the name/email header permanently blank for the session.** `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` are populated only by piggybacking on a successful boot fetch or a successful `setDisplayName()` call; nothing retries if both of `main.dart`'s one-shot boot attempts fail (e.g., app opened offline). *Disposition*: real but narrow (requires offline app launch) — **defer**, propose retrying the fetch the next time Configurações opens rather than relying solely on the two boot-time attempts. — **adversarial lens**

### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed)

Confirmed still present in the current code; logged in `deferred-work.md` under the relevant `spec-8-*` headings. Listed here only because the verification-gap lens independently re-derived the first one with corroborating detail:

- **`clearLocalCache()` not coordinated with in-flight writes/fetches** (`deferred-work.md`, spec-8-4 entry) — the verification-gap lens independently re-confirmed this for `EntriesRepository` (an in-flight `create()`/`retry()` can repopulate the just-cleared box) *and* additionally traced the same shape through `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` (an in-flight fetch, not just a write, can repopulate the just-cleared chat boxes) — broadening, not replacing, the existing entry. **Action item 12** below proposes folding this broader evidence into the existing `deferred-work.md` entry.
- The shared `_finishSession()` re-entry race (logout/deleteAccount/toggleBiometric/confirmEditingName can race each other).
- In-memory singleton state (cached name/email, dashboard aggregate, chat session, pending-write tracker) not reset on logout/delete.
- `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit`'s `confirmedWrites` subscriptions living for the whole app session, not just while mounted.
- Vault PIN never cleared on logout (explicitly flagged as ambiguous, not a defect).
- `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` using `Failure.malformedResponse` for local-storage faults (pre-existing codebase convention).
- No real-DI e2e test for `deleteAccount()`'s full orchestration at the time of spec-8-5's own review — **closed** by the `71b5bdc` closing-snapshot commit, which added exactly this.
- `SessionRepositoryImpl.logout()`'s silent `catch (_) {}` (deliberately mirrors an existing same-file convention).
- The narrative fetch firing unconditionally regardless of entry count (one harmless extra backend call for 0/1-count users) — explicitly accepted in spec-8-2's own Design Notes as the cost of keeping the two `Resource`s genuinely decoupled.

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean.** `grep`-verified: no domain-layer file in `dashboard/` or `account/` imports `package:flutter` or anything from a `data/` layer. All new repository methods return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09). `AccountSettingsCubit` depends only on domain-layer repository interfaces (`SessionRepository`, `VaultRepository`, `EntriesRepository`, `ChatRepository`, `AccountSettingsRepository`) — no cross-feature data-layer imports (RNF06). All five backend calls (`dashboard-aggregate-get`, `dashboard-narrative-get`, `account-settings-update`, `account-delete`, `auth-logout`) match `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping exactly, called by name per AGENTS.md's convention. Zero hardcoded visual values introduced (`grep` for `Color(0x`/raw px literals in the epic's new widget files found none).
- **God-class / size growth.** `account_settings_screen.dart` grew to 677 lines across all 6 commits in this range (net +538 lines over the epic) with a single `build()` method spanning ~354 lines (biometric toggle + dashboard chart + narrative + profile header + name-edit + logout + delete-account, all inline, each story adding its own section without extraction). `account_settings_cubit.dart` grew to 489 lines (net +343) and now owns four largely-unrelated concerns (biometric toggle, name editing, logout, account deletion) in one class. Each story's own in-diff review correctly judged its *own* increment as reasonable; nothing in the per-story process was positioned to notice the cumulative size. The per-line code quality is good — guards, tests, and provenance comments are consistent throughout, confirmed by direct reading — this is a structural/SRP observation, not a correctness defect. **Disposition: accept as-is for this delivery** (no functional requirement calls for splitting it, and extraction now is a refactor with regression risk, not a bug fix); **propose as a follow-up** if this screen gains a 6th concern.
- **Duplication — deliberate, self-documented, by design.** `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit` are near-total structural duplicates (`diff` of the two files shows only the obvious renames/type changes) — but each file's own doc comment explicitly cross-references the other and states the mirroring is intentional per frozen Boundaries text ("mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape"). **Accept as-is** — this is accepted deviation, not an accidental reimplementation from one session not knowing the other existed. The one real cost of the duplication (the identical untested `onError`-handler gap existing in both files) is already tracked in `deferred-work.md`.
- **Spec-to-implementation reconciliation — two real spec bugs caught and fixed, both properly reconciled.** Story 8.1's frozen `>30`-entry condensation algorithm degenerated for `bucketCounts.length < 10` (9 invisible bars + 1 giant bar) — found by review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` (root cause sat inside `<frozen-after-approval>` text), fixed with an explicit Spec Change Log entry (left-pad amendment) per direct human instruction to use technical judgment over the heavier revert-and-replan protocol. Story 8.2's frozen narrative-announcement line was unconditional, in tension with the adjacent "never show narrative for 0/1-count" line — same catch-and-reconcile pattern, same human-routed resolution. Both are exactly the "spec that should be reconciled to reality" case this retro's own catalog describes, and both were *already* reconciled in-story with full evidence trails — no outstanding reconciliation work remains from either.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists for this project (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope, consistent with every story's own Verification section. What was actually exercised in this retro, directly, not from the record alone:

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test` (full suite) — re-ran: **1309/1309 passing**, exactly matching `tests/test-summary.md`'s own final ledger (no drift found this time, unlike the 3 earlier drifts the epic's own stories caught and corrected in-flight).
- The project's real-DI e2e suite (`test/features/account/account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart`, `test/features/dashboard/dashboard_flow_e2e_test.dart`) — the closest thing to an end-to-end behavior check this repo has — exercises the genuine DI graph (`sl<...>()`) with fakes only at the HTTP transport boundary, covering logout, account deletion (happy path, backend failure, double-tap no-op), and dashboard aggregate/narrative fetch+recompute, confirmed read directly as part of the review above.

No manual/visual walkthrough was performed (no device/simulator exists) — this is an explicit scope gap, not "checked and clean," same as every story's own Verification section already states.

## Previous-retro follow-through

No previous retrospective exists for any earlier epic — `sprint-status.yaml` shows `epic-1-retrospective` through `epic-7-retrospective` all still `optional`, none ever run, and there are no `action_items` in the file at all. Nothing to follow through on.

## Action items

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro; the next dev session executes and verifies against the normal `fvm flutter analyze`/`fvm flutter test` gate):

1. **Fix the narrative-error announce dedup bypass** — route the narrative-triggered `BlocListener` (finding 1) through the same `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` state the dashboard-triggered listener already uses, so neither path can re-announce an already-announced, still-failing narrative error. *Owner: dev, next pass on `account_settings_screen.dart`.*
2. **Widen `clearStaleError()` to also clear `deleteAccountErrorMessage`** (finding 2), or add a sibling clear call from `initState()`. *Owner: dev.*
3. **Give `deleteAccount()` its own generation guard** (finding 3), consistent with `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName`. *Owner: dev.*
4. **Add a `catch` to `deleteAccount()`'s cubit method** (finding 4) so an unexpected throw surfaces an error instead of silently resetting state. *Owner: dev.*
5. **Add a retry affordance to the dashboard aggregate's `_errorCard`** (finding 5), matching the narrative section's existing "tentar novamente" link. *Owner: dev.*
6. **Fix `_emptyCard`'s padding** (finding 7) to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding`, matching its sibling cards. *Owner: dev — trivial, one-line.*
7. **Add `semanticsLabel` to the biometric-toggle and name-save spinners** (finding 8), matching the dashboard chart's existing accessibility treatment. *Owner: dev.*

Deferred items (tracked, not blocking, context attached so a later pass doesn't need to re-investigate):

9. Finding 9 (blank/whitespace narrative success falls through both render and announce paths) — low severity; propose treating a blank `ResourceData` the same as the narrative-unavailable case if ever touched again.
10. Finding 10 (unenforced boot-ordering assumption behind `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail`'s one-time read) — revisit only if DI bootstrap ordering changes.
11. Finding 11 (no retry for a failed boot-time name/email fetch) — revisit if offline-launch UX becomes a priority.
12. **Broaden `deferred-work.md`'s existing spec-8-4 `clearLocalCache()`-race entry** to explicitly name `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` repopulation alongside the already-named `create()`/`sendMessage()`/`retryMessage()` — the verification-gap lens traced the fetch-side (not just write-side) manifestation with concrete evidence this retro's Findings section records. *Owner: dev — documentation-only update to the existing ledger entry, not new code.*

Process lessons (what would prevent the next one — no action required unless a future epic recurs):

- **A later story adding a second guard/listener for a concern a prior story already partially solved should diff against the sibling, not just review its own new code.** Findings 1 and 8 are both this shape: a later story's accessibility/dedup fix was added without checking whether an earlier story's own near-identical control already needed, or already had, the same treatment. The per-story 4-layer review process is excellent at catching defects in a story's own diff; it has no step that asks "does a sibling control on this same merged screen already have this, or need this too?" — worth adding as an explicit check the next time a story extends an existing shared screen/cubit rather than building a new one.
- **A story that re-ships an already-deferred gap under a different name should log the recurrence, not leave it silent.** Finding 6 (spec-8-5 reproducing spec-8-4's own already-deferred "no loading indicator" gap without mentioning it) is low-impact here because the underlying disposition is correctly "accept as-is" either way — but the pattern is worth naming: a recurrence of a *known* gap is cheap to flag with one cross-referencing sentence and easy to miss silently once code review assumes "this is new, not a repeat."
- **Worth keeping, not fixing**: the human-routed spec-amendment path (Spec Change Log entries for stories 8.1 and 8.2) worked exactly as intended — two genuinely wrong pieces of *frozen, previously-approved* spec text were caught by post-implementation review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently patched or silently left broken, and resolved with an explicit, evidenced amendment plus a "KEEP" list protecting everything that was already correct. This is the retrospective's own job (catching what no single session could see) already happening *inside* the epic, one story at a time — the fact that two such catches were needed in one five-story epic is itself worth noting for anyone estimating how often frozen spec text needs this safety valve.

## Acceptance verdict

**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria profiled, not declared — epic 8 has no dedicated acceptance-criteria document beyond `epics.md`'s own per-story Given/When/Then text, which this retro treated as the criteria to profile against).

Evidence for "criteria met":
- All three dashboard entry-count states (0/1/>30) implemented, tested, and the one algorithmic defect in the >30 condensation found and fixed in-story with an evidenced spec amendment.
- Narrative text ships as a genuinely independent fetch (never coupled to the chart `Resource`), with a distinct narrative-unavailable state — confirmed by direct code read, not just the spec's own claim.
- Inline name editing matches every I/O-matrix row (pencil→check, save, tap-away revert, failure-keeps-draft) with dedicated widget tests for each.
- Logout calls `auth-logout`, routes to the vault/login screen, and clears both the entries and chat Hive caches (closing the pre-existing shared-device data-leak gap this epic's own spec named as a goal).
- Account deletion uses the destructive-variant red-title dialog, hard-deletes via `DELETE /account`, routes to the same destination as logout, and traps focus while the dialog is open — all confirmed present in code.
- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test`: 1309/1309 passing, re-verified directly in this retro.
- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, RNF09, or design-token violations found anywhere in the epic's diff.

Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 11 new findings (1 real correctness bug surfaced to users — the announce-dedup bypass, finding 1 — the rest are consistency/accessibility/architectural-risk items of lesser severity), none of which represent a failure to deliver the epic's own stated functionality. No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty). No finding rises to "criteria not met."

## Open questions

- Should the already-accepted "no loading indicator on Sair/Apagar conta" gap (findings/deferred item 6, 8) be revisited now that it has recurred twice in the same epic, or does the existing rationale (shared `AppButton` has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify) still hold? This is a product/design call, not something this retro can resolve on its own.

headless: true

# Epic 1 Retrospective — Foundation & Session Management

Epic 1 ("Foundation & Session Management") is the **first** functional unit in the project's delivery order — the scaffold every later epic depends on. It shipped 6 stories across 6 commits:

| Story | Commit | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | `164e1d2` | Project scaffold, stack integration & core infrastructure |
| 1.1 (patch) | `738bf17` | Post-review patches (network pipeline) |
| 1.2 | `1c7fb15` | Design token system & core component library |
| 1.3 | `8a4b944` | Account creation & login |
| 1.4 | `b9870eb` | Silent session refresh & persistence |
| 1.5 + 1.6 | `c35f704` | Expired-session recovery overlay; base navigation shell & feature placeholders |

**Diff range:** `c1706dc..c35f704`. `git_evidence.py` over this range: 6 non-merge commits, 0 merges, 156 files touched, 0 binary revisions.

Automatic per-commit story attribution (`git_evidence.py --stories`) returned an empty `stories` list for every commit — this project's commit subjects spell story numbers as "story 1.5" (period), not the `1-5` hyphen form the script word-matches. Story-to-commit mapping above was done by hand from `git log --oneline --reverse` and is unambiguous (sequential, no overlap).

**Sprint status:** all 6 stories `done`; `sprint_status.py detect-epic --epic 1` confirms `pending_stories: []`, `story_count: 6`, `retro_status: "optional"` before this run.

**Evidence available:** epic spec (`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md` §"Epic 1"), epic context (`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md`), all 6 story spec files, `deferred-work.md`'s per-story entries for spec-1-1 through spec-1-6, current repo state (`fvm flutter analyze`/`fvm flutter test` re-run directly), `git log`/`git diff` over the range above, three parallel review-lens passes (adversarial, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) over the current merged state of the epic's core files (auth, navigation, DI, network pipeline) — reviewed as currently shipped, since epics 2–8 build directly on this code, not frozen at epic 1's own commit boundary.

**Evidence missing:** no session logs exist for this epic's implementation under this machine's `~/.claude/projects/` — process-lesson analysis is sourced from `deferred-work.md`'s self-recorded entries and the specs' own Design Notes/Spec Change Log sections, not a session transcript. This is the **first-ever retrospective run** for this project in sprint mode (epic-1 through epic-7 retrospective keys were all still `optional` before this run). Epic-8's retro (`epic-8-retro-2026-11-08.md`) exists but is chronologically later in delivery order and shares no evidence with epic 1 — not read as a "previous" epic for follow-through purposes.

## Findings

Each finding's disposition is in Action items below. Findings already known and recorded in `deferred-work.md` during the epic's own story-level reviews are listed under "Already known" and not re-routed, except where new evidence changes their status.

### New — seam and currently-live findings (visible only from the merged, now-8-epics-deep state)

Produced by three parallel lens passes over `lib/core/{network,navigation,di,widgets}` and `lib/features/auth/**`, cross-checked against source directly. Deduplicated where two lenses independently found the same defect (noted per item).

1. **Boot-time env validation only checks key presence, not emptiness.** `UrlBuilder` (`lib/core/network/url_builder.dart:16-20`) and `injection_container.dart:27-28` call `dotenv.get(...)` for `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, which throws only if the key is *missing* from `.env` — a `.env` with the keys present but blank (exactly `.env.example`'s own shape, `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL=`) passes silently. *Consequence*: the app boots fully and only fails much later, far less legibly, inside `UrlBuilder.build`/dio — instead of at `main.dart`'s existing catch block, which already prints a friendly "copy .env.example and fill in real values" message purpose-built for exactly this case. — **found independently by edge-case-hunter (both keys separately) and adversarial lens**
2. **An empty-but-non-null access/refresh token is treated as "present."** `header_interceptor.dart:68-70` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` whenever `readAccessToken()` resolves non-null, with no `isNotEmpty` check; `auth_repository_impl.dart:57-64` likewise persists whatever `accessToken`/`refreshToken` strings a signup/login response carries with no non-empty validation before `saveSession`. *Consequence*: an empty-string token from either path is indistinguishable from "no token" at the interceptor, so the backend receives a syntactically-present empty bearer header instead of the request being treated as unauthenticated. — **edge-case-hunter**
3. **Non-idempotent auth POSTs are retried transparently.** `retry_interceptor.dart:74-77`'s `shouldRetry` has no concept of "this POST has no idempotency key and may have already taken effect" — `auth-signup`, `auth-login`, and `auth-refresh` are retried on `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`/`NETWORK_OFFLINE` exactly like any idempotent GET. A later commit (story 6.1) eventually excludes chat/export writes from retry the same way; auth's own writes were never given the same exclusion. *Consequence*: a signup whose response is lost to a timeout gets silently replayed with the identical email/password, surfacing a successful signup as a user-visible failure when the backend rejects the duplicate; worse, `auth-refresh`'s refresh tokens are typically single-use/rotating (`openapi.yaml:177`) — a timed-out-but-actually-successful refresh gets replayed with an already-consumed token, the backend returns `AUTH_INVALID`, and `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()` treats that as a confirmed-dead token and logs out a user whose session was in fact still valid. — **independently found by edge-case-hunter and adversarial lens (adversarial traced the refresh-rotation consequence)**
4. **No redirect away from `/reauth` once the session is genuinely re-authenticated.** `app_router.dart:97-114` has no case for "user is on `/reauth` and `SessionStatus` transitions from `expired` back to `authenticated`" — only forward transitions into `/reauth` are handled. *Consequence*: a user who successfully re-authenticates while on the placeholder reauth screen is stranded there despite being fully authenticated again. — **edge-case-hunter**
5. **Expiry overlay gives up permanently if the overlay context isn't mounted at the exact post-frame callback.** `expiry_overlay_host.dart:99-104`: if `overlayContext` is null when `expired` fires, `_onStatus` resets `_expiryOverlayShown = false` and returns — but `_onSessionExpired()` only emits `expired` on the transition *from* `authenticated`, so once `_lastStatus` is already `expired`, nothing re-arms this path for the rest of that expiry episode. *Consequence*: a race with a Navigator rebuild can leave a user on an authenticated-looking screen with an actually-dead session and zero visual indication, until a manual restart. — **found independently by both edge-case-hunter and adversarial lens (the strongest-corroborated finding in this retro)**
6. **`AuthCubit` has no in-flight-submit guard on `toggleMode`/`emailChanged`/`passwordChanged`.** `auth_cubit.dart:32-63`: none of the three checks `state.isSubmitting` before mutating state. *Consequence*: editing a field or toggling mode while a submit is in flight applies the submit's eventual result (success/error, password-clear) on top of state the user already changed, producing a visibly mismatched mode/email/password. — **edge-case-hunter**
7. **`AuthCubit` is the one cubit in its DI module registered without a `dispose` callback.** `auth_injection.dart:35-48`: `SessionExpiryNotifier` and `SessionRepository` both get explicit `dispose:` callbacks specifically so `sl.reset()` closes their `StreamController`s; `AuthCubit` — itself wrapping a `StreamController` as a `Cubit` — gets none, inconsistent with the file's own stated convention. *Consequence*: every `sl.reset()` call (every test file's teardown) leaks one unclosed `Cubit` instead of releasing it. — **adversarial**
8. **`AuthState.toString()` interpolates the raw password field.** `auth_state.dart:101-104`: `'AuthState(mode: $mode, email: $email, password: $password, ...)'`, re-emitted on every keystroke via `passwordChanged`. *Consequence*: latent today (nothing calls `toString()` on a transition), but the moment any future `BlocObserver`/log line/crash reporter does — a near-universal Flutter debugging pattern — the user's plaintext password starts leaking into logs one keystroke at a time. — **adversarial**
9. **`BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen` has no escape hatch, and the deferral that excused it has not held.** `placeholder_screens.dart:58-70` renders only a centered "Biometria" `Text` — no `AppBar`, no back arrow, no button — unlike every sibling placeholder, which reuses `_BackArrowHeader`. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry explicitly deferred this exact gap on the premise that "Epic 2's real biometric/PIN flow" would replace the screen — but Epic 2 (now shipped) built the app-*launch* vault/PIN gate, a different flow entirely, and never touched this mid-session-expiry placeholder. 10. **`ConfirmationDialog.isOpen`'s deferred risk condition has now arrived.** `confirmation_dialog.dart:57`'s single process-wide static `isOpen` flag gates every `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call across the whole app. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry on this exact flag explicitly named its own trigger condition as "becomes reachable the moment a second consumer is added (Epic 8's account-deletion confirm, by the widget's own doc comment)" — Epic 8 has since shipped exactly that second consumer. *Consequence*: if either dialog's route is ever torn down without completing normally, `isOpen` sticks `true` and silently blocks the *other* feature's confirmation dialog app-wide (e.g., a stuck session-expiry overlay later blocking Epic 8's account-deletion confirm from ever showing), with no connection between the two obvious from either call site. — **adversarial, cross-checked against `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry; reachability of the two consumers actually colliding was not independently re-verified against Epic 8's current call site in this retro**
11. **`dio_error_code.dart`'s mapping folds non-timeout, no-response exception types into the retryable `NETWORK_OFFLINE` code.** `dio_error_code.dart:19-32`: any `DioException` whose `type` isn't one of the four timeout/cancel types and whose `response` is null (e.g. `badCertificate`, `unknown`) falls through to `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. *Consequence*: a deterministic TLS/certificate failure — which fails identically every attempt — gets retried twice before surfacing, reported with the same "you appear offline" messaging as a real connectivity gap, burying a security-relevant signal. — **adversarial**

14. **`access_token_provider.dart`'s documented-safe save/clear ordering has no test covering a partial-write failure.** `saveSession()`/`clearSession()` each write/delete the refresh token before the access token specifically so a mid-sequence failure leaves the system self-healing on next boot (per the file's own code comment) — but every existing test (`access_token_provider_test.dart`, and the fake secure-storage channels in `session_repository_impl_test.dart`/`main_test.dart`) treats every write as unconditionally successful; none asserts call order or exercises a failure between the two writes. *Consequence*: a regression that swapped the write/delete order would not be caught by any existing test, and would, on a real partial secure-storage failure, cause an unwarranted forced logout (`saveSession`) or leave a dead token un-cleared (`clearSession`) instead of the self-healing the ordering exists to guarantee. — **verification-gap**

4. **No redirect away from `/reauth` once the session is genuinely re-authenticated.** `app_router.dart:97-114` has no case for "user is on `/reauth` and `SessionStatus` transitions from `expired` back to `authenticated`" — only forward transitions into `/reauth` are handled. *Consequence*: a user who successfully re-authenticates while on the placeholder reauth screen is stranded there despite being fully authenticated again. — **edge-case-hunter**
5. **Expiry overlay gives up permanently if the overlay context isn't mounted at the exact post-frame callback.** `expiry_overlay_host.dart:99-104`: if `overlayContext` is null when `expired` fires, `_onStatus` resets `_expiryOverlayShown = false` and returns — but `_onSessionExpired()` only emits `expired` on the transition *from* `authenticated`, so once `_lastStatus` is already `expired`, nothing re-arms this path for the rest of that expiry episode. *Consequence*: a race with a Navigator rebuild can leave a user on an authenticated-looking screen with an actually-dead session and zero visual indication, until a manual restart. — **found independently by both edge-case-hunter and adversarial lens (the strongest-corroborated finding in this retro)**
6. **`AuthCubit` has no in-flight-submit guard on `toggleMode`/`emailChanged`/`passwordChanged`.** `auth_cubit.dart:32-63`: none of the three checks `state.isSubmitting` before mutating state. *Consequence*: editing a field or toggling mode while a submit is in flight applies the submit's eventual result (success/error, password-clear) on top of state the user already changed, producing a visibly mismatched mode/email/password. — **edge-case-hunter**
7. **`AuthCubit` is the one cubit in its DI module registered without a `dispose` callback.** `auth_injection.dart:35-48`: `SessionExpiryNotifier` and `SessionRepository` both get explicit `dispose:` callbacks specifically so `sl.reset()` closes their `StreamController`s; `AuthCubit` — itself wrapping a `StreamController` as a `Cubit` — gets none, inconsistent with the file's own stated convention. *Consequence*: every `sl.reset()` call (every test file's teardown) leaks one unclosed `Cubit` instead of releasing it. — **adversarial**
8. **`AuthState.toString()` interpolates the raw password field.** `auth_state.dart:101-104`: `'AuthState(mode: $mode, email: $email, password: $password, ...)'`, re-emitted on every keystroke via `passwordChanged`. *Consequence*: latent today (nothing calls `toString()` on a transition), but the moment any future `BlocObserver`/log line/crash reporter does — a near-universal Flutter debugging pattern — the user's plaintext password starts leaking into logs one keystroke at a time. — **adversarial**
9. **`BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen` has no escape hatch, and the deferral that excused it has not held.** `placeholder_screens.dart:58-70` renders only a centered "Biometria" `Text` — no `AppBar`, no back arrow, no button — unlike every sibling placeholder, which reuses `_BackArrowHeader`. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry explicitly deferred this exact gap on the premise that "Epic 2's real biometric/PIN flow" would replace the screen — but Epic 2 (now shipped) built the app-*launch* vault/PIN gate, a different flow entirely, and never touched this mid-session-expiry placeholder. The deferral's assumed future owner did not materialize. *Consequence*: any user whose session actually expires mid-use and taps the expiry overlay's only button (`widget.router.go(AppRoutePaths.reauth)`) lands on a screen with zero interactive elements. — **adversarial, cross-checked against `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry**
10. **`ConfirmationDialog.isOpen`'s deferred risk condition has now arrived.** `confirmation_dialog.dart:57`'s single process-wide static `isOpen` flag gates every `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call across the whole app. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry on this exact flag explicitly named its own trigger condition as "becomes reachable the moment a second consumer is added (Epic 8's account-deletion confirm, by the widget's own doc comment)" — Epic 8 has since shipped exactly that second consumer. *Consequence*: if either dialog's route is ever torn down without completing normally, `isOpen` sticks `true` and silently blocks the *other* feature's confirmation dialog app-wide (e.g., a stuck session-expiry overlay later blocking Epic 8's account-deletion confirm from ever showing), with no connection between the two obvious from either call site. — **adversarial, cross-checked against `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry; reachability of the two consumers actually colliding was not independently re-verified against Epic 8's current call site in this retro**
11. **`dio_error_code.dart`'s mapping folds non-timeout, no-response exception types into the retryable `NETWORK_OFFLINE` code.** `dio_error_code.dart:19-32`: any `DioException` whose `type` isn't one of the four timeout/cancel types and whose `response` is null (e.g. `badCertificate`, `unknown`) falls through to `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. *Consequence*: a deterministic TLS/certificate failure — which fails identically every attempt — gets retried twice before surfacing, reported with the same "you appear offline" messaging as a real connectivity gap, burying a security-relevant signal. — **adversarial**
12. **A platform exception reading the stored access token is indistinguishable from "no token stored."** `header_interceptor.dart:53-67`'s `catch` around `readAccessToken()` treats any thrown platform exception the same as "nothing stored" — the request proceeds with no `Authorization` header, the backend returns an auth-failure code, and `ApiClient._mapDioException` unconditionally calls `notifyExpired()`. *Consequence*: a transient secure-storage glitch (plausible right after an iOS app resumes from background) is indistinguishable from an actually-dead session — the user sees the full "Sessão expirada" recovery overlay and is pushed to re-authenticate despite a session that was never actually invalid. — **adversarial**
13. **`restoreSession()`'s "never had a session" and "backend confirmed dead token" outcomes share the same `Failure` subtype.** `session_repository_impl.dart:130-139`: a fresh install / post-logout boot with no stored refresh token returns `left(Failure.authExpired(...))` — the identical subtype a backend-confirmed dead token produces a few lines below, even though the two events are semantically distinct. *Consequence*: latent today (nothing currently pattern-matches this `Left`'s subtype), but the first future consumer that does will fire "session expired" messaging on every fresh install, not just a real expiry. — **adversarial**
14. **`access_token_provider.dart`'s documented-safe save/clear ordering has no test covering a partial-write failure.** `saveSession()`/`clearSession()` each write/delete the refresh token before the access token specifically so a mid-sequence failure leaves the system self-healing on next boot (per the file's own code comment) — but every existing test (`access_token_provider_test.dart`, and the fake secure-storage channels in `session_repository_impl_test.dart`/`main_test.dart`) treats every write as unconditionally successful; none asserts call order or exercises a failure between the two writes. *Consequence*: a regression that swapped the write/delete order would not be caught by any existing test, and would, on a real partial secure-storage failure, cause an unwarranted forced logout (`saveSession`) or leave a dead token un-cleared (`clearSession`) instead of the self-healing the ordering exists to guarantee. — **verification-gap**

5. **Expiry overlay gives up permanently if the overlay context isn't mounted at the exact post-frame callback.** `expiry_overlay_host.dart:99-104`: if `overlayContext` is null when `expired` fires, `_onStatus` resets `_expiryOverlayShown = false` and returns — but `_onSessionExpired()` only emits `expired` on the transition *from* `authenticated`, so once `_lastStatus` is already `expired`, nothing re-arms this path for the rest of that expiry episode. *Consequence*: a race with a Navigator rebuild can leave a user on an authenticated-looking screen with an actually-dead session and zero visual indication, until a manual restart. — **found independently by both edge-case-hunter and adversarial lens (the strongest-corroborated finding in this retro)**
6. **`AuthCubit` has no in-flight-submit guard on `toggleMode`/`emailChanged`/`passwordChanged`.** `auth_cubit.dart:32-63`: none of the three checks `state.isSubmitting` before mutating state. *Consequence*: editing a field or toggling mode while a submit is in flight applies the submit's eventual result (success/error, password-clear) on top of state the user already changed, producing a visibly mismatched mode/email/password. — **edge-case-hunter**
7. **`AuthCubit` is the one cubit in its DI module registered without a `dispose` callback.** `auth_injection.dart:35-48`: `SessionExpiryNotifier` and `SessionRepository` both get explicit `dispose:` callbacks specifically so `sl.reset()` closes their `StreamController`s; `AuthCubit` — itself wrapping a `StreamController` as a `Cubit` — gets none, inconsistent with the file's own stated convention. *Consequence*: every `sl.reset()` call (every test file's teardown) leaks one unclosed `Cubit` instead of releasing it. — **adversarial**
8. **`AuthState.toString()` interpolates the raw password field.** `auth_state.dart:101-104`: `'AuthState(mode: $mode, email: $email, password: $password, ...)'`, re-emitted on every keystroke via `passwordChanged`. *Consequence*: latent today (nothing calls `toString()` on a transition), but the moment any future `BlocObserver`/log line/crash reporter does — a near-universal Flutter debugging pattern — the user's plaintext password starts leaking into logs one keystroke at a time. — **adversarial**
9. **`BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen` has no escape hatch, and the deferral that excused it has not held.** `placeholder_screens.dart:58-70` renders only a centered "Biometria" `Text` — no `AppBar`, no back arrow, no button — unlike every sibling placeholder, which reuses `_BackArrowHeader`. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry explicitly deferred this exact gap on the premise that "Epic 2's real biometric/PIN flow" would replace the screen — but Epic 2 (now shipped) built the app-*launch* vault/PIN gate, a different flow entirely, and never touched this mid-session-expiry placeholder. The deferral's assumed future owner did not materialize. *Consequence*: any user whose session actually expires mid-use and taps the expiry overlay's only button (`widget.router.go(AppRoutePaths.reauth)`) lands on a screen with zero interactive elements. — **adversarial, cross-checked against `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry**
10. **`ConfirmationDialog.isOpen`'s deferred risk condition has now arrived.** `confirmation_dialog.dart:57`'s single process-wide static `isOpen` flag gates every `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call across the whole app. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry on this exact flag explicitly named its own trigger condition as "becomes reachable the moment a second consumer is added (Epic 8's account-deletion confirm, by the widget's own doc comment)" — Epic 8 has since shipped exactly that second consumer. *Consequence*: if either dialog's route is ever torn down without completing normally, `isOpen` sticks `true` and silently blocks the *other* feature's confirmation dialog app-wide (e.g., a stuck session-expiry overlay later blocking Epic 8's account-deletion confirm from ever showing), with no connection between the two obvious from either call site. — **adversarial, cross-checked against `deferred-work.md`'s spec-1-5 entry; reachability of the two consumers actually colliding was not independently re-verified against Epic 8's current call site in this retro**
11. **`dio_error_code.dart`'s mapping folds non-timeout, no-response exception types into the retryable `NETWORK_OFFLINE` code.** `dio_error_code.dart:19-32`: any `DioException` whose `type` isn't one of the four timeout/cancel types and whose `response` is null (e.g. `badCertificate`, `unknown`) falls through to `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. *Consequence*: a deterministic TLS/certificate failure — which fails identically every attempt — gets retried twice before surfacing, reported with the same "you appear offline" messaging as a real connectivity gap, burying a security-relevant signal. — **adversarial**
12. **A platform exception reading the stored access token is indistinguishable from "no token stored."** `header_interceptor.dart:53-67`'s `catch` around `readAccessToken()` treats any thrown platform exception the same as "nothing stored" — the request proceeds with no `Authorization` header, the backend returns an auth-failure code, and `ApiClient._mapDioException` unconditionally calls `notifyExpired()`. *Consequence*: a transient secure-storage glitch (plausible right after an iOS app resumes from background) is indistinguishable from an actually-dead session — the user sees the full "Sessão expirada" recovery overlay and is pushed to re-authenticate despite a session that was never actually invalid. — **adversarial**
13. **`restoreSession()`'s "never had a session" and "backend confirmed dead token" outcomes share the same `Failure` subtype.** `session_repository_impl.dart:130-139`: a fresh install / post-logout boot with no stored refresh token returns `left(Failure.authExpired(...))` — the identical subtype a backend-confirmed dead token produces a few lines below, even though the two events are semantically distinct. *Consequence*: latent today (nothing currently pattern-matches this `Left`'s subtype), but the first future consumer that does will fire "session expired" messaging on every fresh install, not just a real expiry. — **adversarial**
14. **`access_token_provider.dart`'s documented-safe save/clear ordering has no test covering a partial-write failure.** `saveSession()`/`clearSession()` each write/delete the refresh token before the access token specifically so a mid-sequence failure leaves the system self-healing on next boot (per the file's own code comment) — but every existing test (`access_token_provider_test.dart`, and the fake secure-storage channels in `session_repository_impl_test.dart`/`main_test.dart`) treats every write as unconditionally successful; none asserts call order or exercises a failure between the two writes. *Consequence*: a regression that swapped the write/delete order would not be caught by any existing test, and would, on a real partial secure-storage failure, cause an unwarranted forced logout (`saveSession`) or leave a dead token un-cleared (`clearSession`) instead of the self-healing the ordering exists to guarantee. — **verification-gap**
