# Epic 4 Retrospective — Entry List, Sync Badge, Empty State, Entry Detail

Epic 4 shipped 4 stories across 4 commits:

| Story | Commit | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | `5b3ba87` | Chronological entry list with origin marking |
| 4.2 | `526b6bf` | Per-entry sync badge |
| 4.3 | `aed0a39` | Empty-state handling; story 4.2 round-2 review fixes |
| 4.4 | `eaa00bc` | Entry detail view; story 4.3 round-2 review fixes |

**Diff range:** `5b3ba87^..eaa00bc`. `git_evidence.py`: 4 non-merge commits, 58 files touched, 8740 insertions.

**Sprint status:** `detect-epic --epic 4` confirms `story_count: 4`, `pending_stories: []`, `retro_status: "optional"` before this run.

**Evidence available:** epic spec (`epics.md` §"Epic 4"), `epic-4-context.md`, all 4 story specs, `deferred-work.md`'s spec-4-1 through spec-4-4 entries (unusually dense — 20+ items, this epic's own reviews were thorough), current repo state (`fvm flutter analyze`, targeted test re-run), three parallel review-lens passes over `lib/features/entries/presentation/**` and `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart`.

**Evidence missing:** no session logs. Epics 1-3's retrospectives (all finalized earlier in this sweep) are the previous retros — see Previous-retro follow-through.

## Findings

### New — currently-live findings, most severe first

1. **`PendingEntryWriteTracker` is never cleared at any session boundary — the most severe finding in this entire retrospective sweep.** It is a DI-singleton holding, in memory, the full plaintext `content` of every in-flight or failed capture (`pending_entry_write.dart:74`), shared across `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` and surfaced through `MeusRegistrosCubit`. `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()` — the only place any session-ending cleanup happens — calls `EntriesRepository.clearLocalCache()`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` (Epic 3's own fix target) but never touches the tracker; `sl.reset()` is confirmed, by repo-wide grep, to never run from any production code path. *Consequence — three distinct, confirmed mechanisms*: (a) User B's "Meus Registros" shows User A's still-pending or failed entry as a phantom card, exposing User A's actual private journal text — the app's core sensitive content — to User B; (b) if User A's write resolves successfully after User A has already logged out, `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl._resolve()` broadcasts it and `MeusRegistrosCubit._onEntryConfirmed()` permanently prepends it into **User B's** own list; (c) if User B taps the stale error badge's retry affordance, it replays `_repository.create()` with **User A's original content** — `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create()` takes no explicit user id and relies purely on the ambient Authorization header for whichever session is currently active, so this writes User A's journal content to the backend **as a new entry on User B's account** — a genuine cross-account content-injection path, not merely a display glitch. — **adversarial lens**; directly extends Epic 3's own action item 1 (which proposed the same session-boundary wiring for the two repository caches) — this tracker needs the identical treatment.
2. **`EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`/`search()` have no per-item parse isolation — unlike every other decode path in this same feature.** `data.map((item) => EntryDto.fromJson(...)).toList()` is one expression inside one try/catch spanning the whole page; one malformed item (a null/missing field, or a `source` value the client doesn't yet recognize) discards every already-parsed item in that page. `entry_date_group.dart` and `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s own Hive-cache paths already skip one corrupt item rather than failing outright (documented RNF09 rationale) — this inconsistency is specific to the two remote-fetch paths. *Consequence*: `Failure.malformedResponse` isn't one of the two types the offline fallback absorbs, so this surfaces as a hard error on the first page or a permanently-poisoned cursor on `loadMore()` — one bad entry anywhere in a page hides every otherwise-good entry on it, forever, since retrying re-fetches the same page. — **edge-case-hunter**
3. **A tempId-keyed detail view for a still-pending entry shows "Registro não encontrado" immediately and never self-corrects.** `EntryRecordCard`/`MeusRegistrosScreen` explicitly route a pending placeholder's synthetic tempId into the same `onCardTap`→`getById` path "with no branching." Since the tempId was never registered server-side, `getById` always resolves `NotFound`. `EntryDetailCubit` never subscribes to `_tracker.confirmedWrites`, so even if the real write confirms moments later while the screen is still open, nothing re-fetches or corrects the displayed state. *Consequence*: a user who taps a "Sincronizando" card is shown a misleading not-found message for content that may well succeed within moments, with no self-correction short of backing out and re-opening the (now different, server-id-keyed) card. — **edge-case-hunter**
4. **`EntryDetailCubit`'s `pendingWrites` subscription only mutates a field — it never calls `emit`.** Contrasted directly with the same class's `_onSessionStatusChanged`, which does call `emit` on every tick. *Consequence*: if a user opens the detail view of an entry already showing a `synchronizing`/`error` badge, and that write's status subsequently changes while the screen stays open, the badge is frozen at whatever it was when `load()` last ran — it never flips to "Sincronizado" or an error — until the user navigates away and back. Compounds finding 3: even once finding 3 is fixed to re-fetch on confirmation, this gap means any status change *before* a full re-fetch triggers still renders stale. — **verification-gap**
5. **`PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()` drops every existing failed write tracker-wide, not just the one it's replacing.** The code's own comment justifies this only for the single-modal, same-attempt retry case, but `_pending.removeWhere((_, write) => write.status is PendingEntryWriteFailed)` sweeps *all* failed records regardless of lineage — and since the tracker is one lazySingleton shared across Texto/Áudio/Foto, a failed text entry is silently wiped the moment the user later records an unrelated photo or audio entry. Since the tracker is purely in-memory, the original content is then unrecoverable. *Consequence*: a previously-failed entry's error card vanishes from Meus Registros with no warning and no way to retry it, the instant an unrelated capture is attempted. — **edge-case-hunter**; escalates `deferred-work.md`'s spec-4-2-round-2 entry (which framed this as a product question about lineage-scoping) with concrete cross-cubit evidence that makes it a correctness bug, not just an open design question.

### Already known, escalated to fix-now on new evidence

6. **`MeusRegistrosCubit.loadFirstPage()`'s failure branch silently swallows a real load error whenever a pending write exists**, emitting an empty `MeusRegistrosLoaded` instead of `MeusRegistrosError` — no message, no "Tentar novamente," and any previously-displayed entries are already gone from state (every `loadFirstPage()` emits `MeusRegistrosLoading` first). `deferred-work.md`'s spec-4-3 entry already flags this, found independently by two review layers, as "a plausible real data-loss-looking UX regression" — still unfixed and unexercised by any test combining a pending write with a failing reload from an already-loaded state.
7. **"Criar primeiro registro"'s CTA has no debounce/in-flight guard** — a rapid double-tap opens two stacked Insertion Modal instances. `deferred-work.md`'s spec-4-3 entry notes this reproduces the identical, already-shipped, unguarded pattern on the Home/Chat FAB, and recommends fixing both call sites together.

### Verification gaps (behavior correct today, unguarded against regression)

8. **The one-frame double-placeholder/confirmed-entry de-dup fix is only proven against a fake tracker with no `Stream.multi` hop** — the real tracker-plus-real-cubit e2e test never asserts intermediate stream emissions, only final settled state. A regression in the real stream-wrapping/ordering could silently reintroduce the double-render the fix exists to prevent.
9. **The documented "a killed app loses every pending write, by design" claim is pure assertion** — no test exercises an actual DI reset/rebuild cycle to prove it (every `resetCoreDependencies()` call in the suite is for per-test isolation, never to check this specific claim).
10. **`MeusRegistrosCubit`'s `isClosed` guards in `_loadFiltered`/`_fetchMore` are untested independently of the adjacent generation guard** — the same Epic-2-recurring pattern ("isClosed guards tested for some methods, not their siblings"), and notably `EntryDetailCubit` (shipped in this same epic) *does* have the direct close-before-resolve test `MeusRegistrosCubit` lacks for the identically-shaped guard.

### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed beyond items 6-7 above)

Grouped by theme — all confirmed still present, none newly discovered:

- **Performance / unbounded growth** (no ceiling, not correctness bugs): the `entries` Hive box grows forever with no eviction; `MeusRegistrosLoaded.groups`/`badgeFor()`/`_displayEntries()` all recompute from scratch on every access including footer-only pagination rebuilds. Already flagged to revisit "once a real dataset-size problem is observed, likely around Epic 5/8" — both have since shipped; not independently re-verified here whether the problem has materialized.
- **Duplication**: `_formatLocalDateTime` (entry detail) vs. `_formatTime` (entry card) — two independent same-shape date-fallback implementations; `_cachedEntryOrOriginalFailure` duplicates `_offlineFallback`'s decode logic; hand-rolled `==`/`hashCode`/`toString` on four value classes with no shared base; six-plus hand-written `EntriesRepository` test fakes.
- **Accessibility** (consistent with the same recurring gap in Epics 1/3): `EntryRecordCard`'s origin icon, the newly-tappable card itself, and the "Registro não encontrado" view all lack `Semantics` labels beyond default widget behavior.
- **Minor test-coverage gaps**, bundled: the all-malformed-`occurredAt` empty-state fallback has no widget test; `_displayEntries.reversed` is untested with 2+ concurrent pending writes; the `ValueKey(entry.id)` fix preventing badge-state leak across reordered cards has no regression test; `list()`/`_offlineFallback()` are only tested against a `MockBox`, never real Hive; `app_router_test.dart`'s new nested route only covers the authenticated happy path; `ExpiryOverlayHost` rendering above a live `EntryDetailScreen` is untested end-to-end (only generically elsewhere).
- **Minor / low-priority**: `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()`'s `startedAt` has no injectable clock seam; `EntryDetailCubit`'s pending-write-tempId-matching code is provably unreachable in production (a `getById` success can never equal a synthetic tempId); `pendingWrites`/`statusStream` subscriptions app-wide have no `onError` handler (cross-cutting, not specific to this epic).
- **`Failure.message` rendered verbatim with raw-English fallback strings** — the same recurring gap Epic 1's retrospective already promoted to a fix-now action item (building the `Failure`→localized-copy mapping layer); this epic's own spec-4-1 entry is one more confirmed recurrence, not a new item.

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean.** No `domain/` file in `lib/features/entries/` imports `package:flutter` or `data/` (RNF06). All repository/service methods return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09). Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- **A new, uncatalogued midnight-boundary date-grouping edge case** (from the edge-case-hunter lens): a pending write started just before local midnight groups under "Hoje" using the client's own `startedAt`, but the server assigns its own `occurredAt` on receipt, which can cross into the next calendar day under normal latency. Once confirmed, the entry re-groups under an unlabeled future date, appearing to jump out of "Hoje." Narrow window, self-corrects on the next full reload; not independently verified on a device. See Action items.
- **Spec-to-implementation note**: `create()`'s tracker-wide failed-write drop (finding 5) is technically a correct implementation of spec-4-2's frozen Boundaries text as literally written — the gap is that the text's own stated rationale (same-modal retry) is narrower than what it authorizes. Flagged as both a bug (given the cross-cubit, unrecoverable-content consequence) and an open product question about whether tracker-wide dropping was ever actually intended.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope. Finding 1's full real-world reachability (two actual accounts on one physical device) and the midnight-boundary grouping glitch could not be directly observed.

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test test/features/entries/presentation test/features/entries/domain/services` — re-ran: **182/182 passing**.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Epics 1-3's retrospectives (33 action items total, all `status: open`) were all finalized earlier in this same sweep. No dev session has touched the code between any of those finalizations and this retro starting; nothing could plausibly have landed. Recorded as "no evidence of landing," not "not done." No `--set-action-status` proposals from this epic's review.

## Action items

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro):

1. Wire `PendingEntryWriteTracker.reset()` (new method: clear `_pending`, re-emit an empty snapshot, don't close controllers) into the exact same session-boundary points Epic 3's action item 1 already named — `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`, `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`'s dead-token branch, `AuthCubit.submit()`'s success path (finding 1). *Owner: dev — highest-priority item in this entire retrospective sweep: confirmed cross-account content exposure and content-injection.*
2. Add per-item parse isolation to `EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`/`search()`, matching the pattern `entry_date_group.dart`/the Hive-cache paths already use (finding 2). *Owner: dev.*
3. Give `EntryDetailCubit` a `confirmedWrites` subscription so a tempId-keyed detail view re-resolves once the underlying write actually lands, instead of permanently showing "Registro não encontrado" (finding 3). *Owner: dev.*
4. Make `EntryDetailCubit`'s `pendingWrites` subscription call `emit`, not just mutate a field, so an open detail view's sync badge updates live (finding 4). *Owner: dev — pairs naturally with item 3.*
5. Scope `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()`'s failed-record drop to the write it's actually superseding (`supersedesTempId`), not every failed write tracker-wide (finding 5). *Owner: dev.*
6. Fix `loadFirstPage()`'s failure branch to surface a real `MeusRegistrosError` (with retry) instead of silently discarding previously-loaded entries, when a pending write happens to also exist (already-known item 6). *Owner: dev.*
7. Add a debounce/in-flight guard to "Criar primeiro registro"'s `onPressed`, and the identical unguarded Home/Chat FAB (already-known item 7). *Owner: dev — covers both call sites together, per `deferred-work.md`'s own recommendation.*

Deferred items (tracked, context attached):

8. Finding 8 (double-render de-dup only proven against a fake, no-`Stream.multi` tracker) — add a real-tracker-plus-real-cubit test asserting intermediate stream emissions.
9. Finding 9 ("killed app loses pending writes" is asserted, not tested) — add a test exercising an actual DI reset/rebuild cycle.
10. Finding 10 (`MeusRegistrosCubit`'s `isClosed` guards untested independently of the generation guard) — add the close-before-resolve test `EntryDetailCubit` already has for the same-shaped guard.
11. The midnight-boundary date-grouping jump (aggregate views) — narrow window, self-corrects on next reload; propose anchoring the confirmed entry's displayed group to the pending write's own `startedAt` day if this proves disruptive in practice.
12. Performance cluster (unbounded Hive box growth, unbounded `groups`/`badgeFor`/`_displayEntries` recompute) — revisit now that Epics 5 and 8 (both flagged as the likely trigger) have shipped; not independently re-verified whether a real problem has materialized.
13. Duplication cluster (date-formatting, offline-decode logic, hand-rolled equality, hand-written fakes) — revisit once a third consumer needs the same shape.
14. Accessibility cluster (`EntryRecordCard`, tappable card, not-found view — no `Semantics`) — revisit with a deliberate accessibility pass, same recurring theme as Epics 1/3.
15. Remaining minor test-coverage gaps (malformed-`occurredAt` empty-state widget test, 2+-concurrent-pending-writes `.reversed` test, `ValueKey` badge-leak regression test, real-Hive round-trip for `list()`/`_offlineFallback`, `app_router_test` unauthenticated/cold-deep-link coverage, `ExpiryOverlayHost`-above-detail e2e) — bundle as one cleanup pass.
16. `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()`'s `startedAt` clock seam, `EntryDetailCubit`'s unreachable tempId-matching dead code, and the app-wide missing `onError` handlers on `pendingWrites`/`statusStream` subscriptions — low priority, revisit together if any of these proves reachable.

Process lessons:

- **A tracker/service holding sensitive in-memory state needs session-boundary cleanup audited at the same time its owning repository's cache-clear is fixed, not as a separate afterthought.** Epic 3's own retro proposed the cache-clear fix for `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository`; `PendingEntryWriteTracker` is a sibling DI-singleton added one epic later holding equally sensitive data, and nothing cross-checked whether the same fix needed to cover it too. When fixing a session-boundary gap, grep for every other DI-singleton in the same feature area before considering the fix complete.
- **A deferred item framed as "a product question, not a bug" should be re-examined once a second, more severe consequence of the same code is found.** Finding 5 (tracker-wide failed-write drop) was originally filed as a spec-interpretation question; the edge-case-hunter lens's cross-cubit framing turns it into a straightforward data-loss bug. The lesson isn't that the original framing was wrong — it was a defensible call given what was known then — but that "accept as a product question" dispositions should be revisited whenever new evidence changes the severity, not left permanently closed.

## Acceptance verdict

**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria declared — `epics.md` §"Epic 4" gives explicit Given/When/Then per story).

Evidence for "criteria met":
- Chronological entry list with origin marking, per-entry sync badge, empty-state handling, and entry detail view all implemented and exercised by a large test suite.
- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test` (entries presentation + services scope): 182/182 passing, re-verified directly.
- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, or RNF09 violations found anywhere in the epic's code.
- No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty).

Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 5 new findings (one — the uncleared `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — is a confirmed, serious cross-account content-exposure-and-injection vulnerability; the rest are real but narrower UX/correctness bugs), 2 already-known items escalated to fix-now on review, 3 verification gaps, plus a large but low-severity backlog of performance/duplication/accessibility items this epic's own thorough story-level reviews already catalogued. None represents a failure to deliver this epic's own declared list/badge/detail functionality — but finding 1's severity is high enough that it should not wait for a future epic to surface on its own.

## Open questions

- Is tracker-wide failed-write dropping (finding 5) ever actually the *intended* behavior — e.g. a deliberate "only one error banner at a time" simplification — or was the frozen spec text's own rationale (same-modal retry) the real intent all along, making this a straightforward bug? This retro treats it as a bug given the unrecoverable-content consequence, but the original spec author's intent wasn't re-confirmed with a human.
- Now that Epic 3's cache-clear fix and this epic's tracker-reset fix (action items 1) will both touch `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`/`SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`/`AuthCubit.submit()`, should these three session-boundary cleanup calls be consolidated into one explicit "wipe all per-account client state" chokepoint, rather than each repository/service being wired in separately as its own gap is found? This is the architectural question Epic 3's own retro already raised; Epic 4's evidence reinforces it with a second, independent occurrence of the same shape.

## Assumptions

- **Epic selection:** `-H 4`, continuing the same multi-epic headless sweep. Confirmed via `detect-epic --epic 4`: `story_count: 4`, `pending_stories: []`.
- **No human confirmation was sought** for any step; headless end-to-end. Team discussion (Phase 3) not invoked.
- **Verdict rendered from evidence alone**: **accepted-with-open-items** — criteria met, named findings deferred/tracked, no unfinished stories. The severity of finding 1 was weighed but, per the rubric, does not on its own force a **rejected** verdict (that requires a blocking finding against *this epic's own* declared criteria or unfinished stories, neither of which applies) — it is recorded as the most urgent open item instead.
- **The escalation of items 6/7 from "deferred" to "fix-now," and of finding 5 from "product question" to "bug," were made from the new cross-epic/cross-cubit evidence directly, without a human confirming the reinterpretation.**

- **Minor test-coverage gaps**, bundled: the all-malformed-`occurredAt` empty-state fallback has no widget test; `_displayEntries.reversed` is untested with 2+ concurrent pending writes; the `ValueKey(entry.id)` fix preventing badge-state leak across reordered cards has no regression test; `list()`/`_offlineFallback()` are only tested against a `MockBox`, never real Hive; `app_router_test.dart`'s new nested route only covers the authenticated happy path; `ExpiryOverlayHost` rendering above a live `EntryDetailScreen` is untested end-to-end (only generically elsewhere).
- **Minor / low-priority**: `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()`'s `startedAt` has no injectable clock seam; `EntryDetailCubit`'s pending-write-tempId-matching code is provably unreachable in production (a `getById` success can never equal a synthetic tempId); `pendingWrites`/`statusStream` subscriptions app-wide have no `onError` handler (cross-cutting, not specific to this epic).
- **`Failure.message` rendered verbatim with raw-English fallback strings** — the same recurring gap Epic 1's retrospective already promoted to a fix-now action item (building the `Failure`→localized-copy mapping layer); this epic's own spec-4-1 entry is one more confirmed recurrence, not a new item.

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean.** No `domain/` file in `lib/features/entries/` imports `package:flutter` or `data/` (RNF06). All repository/service methods return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09). Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- **A new, uncatalogued midnight-boundary date-grouping edge case** (from the edge-case-hunter lens): a pending write started just before local midnight groups under "Hoje" using the client's own `startedAt`, but the server assigns its own `occurredAt` on receipt, which can cross into the next calendar day under normal latency. Once confirmed, the entry re-groups under an unlabeled future date, appearing to jump out of "Hoje." Narrow window, self-corrects on the next full reload; not independently verified on a device. See Action items.
- **Spec-to-implementation note**: `create()`'s tracker-wide failed-write drop (finding 5) is technically a correct implementation of spec-4-2's frozen Boundaries text as literally written — the gap is that the text's own stated rationale (same-modal retry) is narrower than what it authorizes. Flagged as both a bug (given the cross-cubit, unrecoverable-content consequence) and an open product question about whether tracker-wide dropping was ever actually intended.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope. Finding 1's full real-world reachability (two actual accounts on one physical device) and the midnight-boundary grouping glitch could not be directly observed.

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test test/features/entries/presentation test/features/entries/domain/services` — re-ran: **182/182 passing**.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Epics 1-3's retrospectives (33 action items total, all `status: open`) were all finalized earlier in this same sweep. No dev session has touched the code between any of those finalizations and this retro starting; nothing could plausibly have landed. Recorded as "no evidence of landing," not "not done." No `--set-action-status` proposals from this epic's review.

## Action items

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro):

1. Wire `PendingEntryWriteTracker.reset()` (new method: clear `_pending`, re-emit an empty snapshot, don't close controllers) into the exact same session-boundary points Epic 3's action item 1 already named — `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`, `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`'s dead-token branch, `AuthCubit.submit()`'s success path (finding 1). *Owner: dev — highest-priority item in this entire retrospective sweep: confirmed cross-account content exposure and content-injection.*
2. Add per-item parse isolation to `EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`/`search()`, matching the pattern `entry_date_group.dart`/the Hive-cache paths already use (finding 2). *Owner: dev.*
3. Give `EntryDetailCubit` a `confirmedWrites` subscription so a tempId-keyed detail view re-resolves once the underlying write actually lands, instead of permanently showing "Registro não encontrado" (finding 3). *Owner: dev.*
4. Make `EntryDetailCubit`'s `pendingWrites` subscription call `emit`, not just mutate a field, so an open detail view's sync badge updates live (finding 4). *Owner: dev — pairs naturally with item 3.*
5. Scope `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()`'s failed-record drop to the write it's actually superseding (`supersedesTempId`), not every failed write tracker-wide (finding 5). *Owner: dev.*
6. Fix `loadFirstPage()`'s failure branch to surface a real `MeusRegistrosError` (with retry) instead of silently discarding previously-loaded entries, when a pending write happens to also exist (already-known item 6). *Owner: dev.*
7. Add a debounce/in-flight guard to "Criar primeiro registro"'s `onPressed`, and the identical unguarded Home/Chat FAB (already-known item 7). *Owner: dev — covers both call sites together, per `deferred-work.md`'s own recommendation.*

Deferred items (tracked, context attached):

8. Finding 8 (double-render de-dup only proven against a fake, no-`Stream.multi` tracker) — add a real-tracker-plus-real-cubit test asserting intermediate stream emissions.
9. Finding 9 ("killed app loses pending writes" is asserted, not tested) — add a test exercising an actual DI reset/rebuild cycle.
10. Finding 10 (`MeusRegistrosCubit`'s `isClosed` guards untested independently of the generation guard) — add the close-before-resolve test `EntryDetailCubit` already has for the same-shaped guard.
11. The midnight-boundary date-grouping jump (aggregate views) — narrow window, self-corrects on next reload; propose anchoring the confirmed entry's displayed group to the pending write's own `startedAt` day if this proves disruptive in practice.
12. Performance cluster (unbounded Hive box growth, unbounded `groups`/`badgeFor`/`_displayEntries` recompute) — revisit now that Epics 5 and 8 (both flagged as the likely trigger) have shipped; not independently re-verified whether a real problem has materialized.
13. Duplication cluster (date-formatting, offline-decode logic, hand-rolled equality, hand-written fakes) — revisit once a third consumer needs the same shape.
14. Accessibility cluster (`EntryRecordCard`, tappable card, not-found view — no `Semantics`) — revisit with a deliberate accessibility pass, same recurring theme as Epics 1/3.

Remaining minor test-coverage gaps (malformed-`occurredAt` empty-state widget test, 2+-concurrent-pending-writes `.reversed` test, `ValueKey` badge-leak regression test, real-Hive round-trip for `list()`/`_offlineFallback`, `app_router_test` unauthenticated/cold-deep-link coverage, `ExpiryOverlayHost`-above-detail e2e) — bundle as one cleanup pass.

- **A tracker/service holding sensitive in-memory state needs session-boundary cleanup audited at the same time its owning repository's cache-clear is fixed, not as a separate afterthought.** Epic 3's own retro proposed the cache-clear fix for `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository`; `PendingEntryWriteTracker` is a sibling DI-singleton added one epic later holding equally sensitive data, and nothing cross-checked whether the same fix needed to cover it too. When fixing a session-boundary gap, grep for every other DI-singleton in the same feature area before considering the fix complete.
- **A deferred item framed as "a product question, not a bug" should be re-examined once a second, more severe consequence of the same code is found.** Finding 5 (tracker-wide failed-write drop) was originally filed as a spec-interpretation question; the edge-case-hunter lens's cross-cubit framing turns it into a straightforward data-loss bug. The lesson isn't that the original framing was wrong — it was a defensible call given what was known then — but that "accept as a product question" dispositions should be revisited whenever new evidence changes the severity, not left permanently closed.

**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria declared — `epics.md` §"Epic 4" gives explicit Given/When/Then per story).

Evidence for "criteria met":
- Chronological entry list with origin marking, per-entry sync badge, empty-state handling, and entry detail view all implemented and exercised by a large test suite.
- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test` (entries presentation + services scope): 182/182 passing, re-verified directly.
- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, or RNF09 violations found anywhere in the epic's code.
- No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty).

Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 5 new findings (one — the uncleared `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — is a confirmed, serious cross-account content-exposure-and-injection vulnerability; the rest are real but narrower UX/correctness bugs), 2 already-known items escalated to fix-now on review, 3 verification gaps, plus a large but low-severity backlog of performance/duplication/accessibility items this epic's own thorough story-level reviews already catalogued. ## Open questions

- Is tracker-wide failed-write dropping (finding 5) ever actually the *intended* behavior — e.g. a deliberate "only one error banner at a time" simplification — or was the frozen spec text's own rationale (same-modal retry) the real intent all along, making this a straightforward bug? This is the architectural question Epic 3's own retro already raised; Epic 4's evidence reinforces it with a second, independent occurrence of the same shape.

---
epic: 5

# Epic 5 Retrospective — Semantic Search, Metadata Filters, Combined Search+Filter

Epic 5 shipped 3 stories across 3 commits:

| Story | Commit | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | `6e4e9d5` | Semantic search with debounced input (backend `entries-search`, the only AI-provider-backed feature in this epic) |
| 5.2 | `afb4d31` | Metadata filters; story 5.1 round-2 review fixes |
| 5.3 | `9dd6fdf` | Combined search + filter & non-disruptive clearing; story 5.2 round-2 review fixes |

**Diff range:** `6e4e9d5^..9dd6fdf`. `git_evidence.py`: 3 non-merge commits, 34 files touched, 6424 insertions.

**Sprint status:** `detect-epic --epic 5` confirms `story_count: 3`, `pending_stories: []`, `retro_status: "optional"` before this run.

**Evidence available:** epic spec (`epics.md` §"Epic 5"), `epic-5-context.md`, all 3 story specs, `deferred-work.md`'s spec-5-1 through spec-5-3 entries (6 items, fairly contained), current repo state, three parallel review-lens passes over `EntriesSearchCubit`, `EntriesFilterSheet`, and their wiring into `MeusRegistrosScreen`.

**Evidence missing:** no session logs. Epics 1-4's retrospectives (49 action items total) are the previous retros — see Previous-retro follow-through.

## Findings

### New — currently-live findings, most severe first

1. **`EntriesSearchCubit` is never cleared at any session boundary — the fourth consecutive epic in this sweep to surface this exact shape.** It is a DI `lazySingleton` (deliberately, so a query "survives leaving and re-entering `/meus-registros`") holding a live `Resource` of real search-result content (entry titles/snippets). `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()` clears only the entries/chat Hive caches (Epic 3's fix target) and, now, should clear `PendingEntryWriteTracker` (Epic 4's fix target) — it never touches this cubit, and `sl.reset()` is confirmed to never run from production code. `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState()` does call `updateFilters(source: null, ...)` unconditionally on every mount, but `updateFilters()`'s own "skip when unchanged" short-circuit treats the common no-filter case as a no-op, so User A's stale search results are never re-queried or cleared. *Consequence*: on a shared/handed-off device, a different account's real journal-entry content (titles/snippets returned by semantic search) renders directly to the next logged-in user — a cross-account privacy breach, the same shape as Epic 2's PIN finding, Epic 3's cache finding, and Epic 4's tracker finding, now confirmed a fourth time in a fourth consecutive epic. — **adversarial lens**
2. **The search box renders empty after a screen remount while the search surface keeps showing a stale, active search — a confirmed dead end, not just a cosmetic gap.** `EntriesSearchBar`'s `TextField` has no `controller`/`initialValue`; `MeusRegistrosScreen`'s teardown/rebuild (tab switch away and back, or navigating into entry detail and back — the plain `GoRoute` for `/meus-registros` tears down the whole subtree, acknowledged by the screen's own remount-skeleton-timer guard) discards the visible text but not the cubit's retained `Resource`/query. *Consequence*: the user sees search results (or a lingering error/skeleton) with an apparently blank, unused-looking search box, and no obvious way back to the plain timeline — the empty box has nothing to delete to trigger the documented "empty query reverts to timeline" recovery path, and "Limpar filtros" doesn't clear search either. — **independently found by both the edge-case-hunter and adversarial lenses**, and sharpens `deferred-work.md`'s own spec-5-1 entry (which flagged the stale-results-with-empty-box symptom but not that it's a genuine dead end) from "worth a look" to a confirmed bug.
3. **A fast-typing user can see a flash of stale search results for an already-abandoned query term.** `onQueryChanged` cancels and restarts the debounce timer on every keystroke but does **not** bump `_generation` — that counter only advances on clear-to-empty or inside `_search()` once a debounce actually fires. If query A's network call resolves before query B's fresh 300ms debounce elapses (plausible on a fast backend), A's result still passes the `generation != _generation` guard (unchanged) and renders — momentarily overwriting the screen with results for a term the user has already typed past. *Consequence*: contradicts the story's own "exactly one call, for the final value" guarantee at the display level; not covered by the existing "stale response" tests, which only exercise the case where the *second* query's debounce has already fired before the first resolves. — **edge-case-hunter**
4. **Superseded search requests are never actually cancelled — only their results are discarded.** No `CancelToken` exists anywhere in `ApiClient.get()`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()`/`EntriesRepositoryImpl.search()`/`EntriesSearchCubit`. A fast-typing or rapid filter-toggling session (story 5.3's own immediate re-search-on-filter-change, no debounce) fires overlapping `entries-search` calls; the generation guard correctly drops the superseded *result*, but the request still runs to completion server-side. *Consequence*: given `openapi.yaml`'s own note that `entries-search` has "no server-side throttle," every superseded-but-not-cancelled search still triggers a full, billable embedding-generation call that is always discarded — a real AI-provider cost multiplier, directly in scope of the project's "every AI feature goes through the backend" cost accountability, not a correctness bug. — **adversarial lens**

### Confirmed clean (explicitly checked, worth recording as a negative result)

- **Retry-safety of `entries-search` is genuinely correct and genuinely tested.** It's a GET, correctly excluded from nothing (unlike the non-idempotent POSTs `RetryInterceptor` already excludes), and retrying it on `EMBEDDING_FAILED`/`RATE_LIMITED`/`NETWORK_TIMEOUT` is the intended policy (AD-4) — verified against `error-taxonomy.md`. A dedicated e2e test (`entries_search_flow_e2e_test.dart`) queues real repeated 503s through the real `RetryInterceptor` and passes. Out-of-order results from a slow retry chain are also safe: the generation guard is checked on every resolution regardless of retry duration.
- **The generation guard correctly discards a stale result racing a filter-clear**, confirmed by direct trace of every interleaving and backed by a dedicated passing test. The real desync in this area lives at the UI-state level (findings 2-3), not in the generation guard itself.

### Verification gaps (behavior correct today, unguarded against regression)

5. **`onQueryChanged('')` called after `cubit.close()` is the one `isClosed` guard in this file untested independently of its two siblings** — the existing close()-adjacent tests cover the async-search-in-flight guard and the `updateFilters()`-after-close guard, but not this synchronous empty-branch one.
6. **The cubit's advertised "query survives leaving and re-entering the screen" singleton behavior is never actually tested** — `bootstrap_integration_test.dart` only checks resolvability, not instance identity across two resolutions, and `app_router_test.dart`'s own test registers a fake with a comment self-disclosing "this suite never exercises a real search."
7. **The combined search+filter race (story 5.3's own subject) is only tested at the isolated cubit level with genuine concurrent timing — never through the real widget wiring.** Every widget/screen-level combined test waits for the search to fully settle before touching the filter sheet; no test taps a filter chip or "Aplicar" while the debounce timer is still pending or the search future is unresolved through the actual `EntriesSearchBar`→`EntriesSearchCubit`→`EntriesFilterSheet`→`MeusRegistrosScreen` wiring.

### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed beyond finding 2 above)

- `search()`'s DTO→Entity mapping runs outside the method's own try/catch, so an exception there would escape unmapped — pre-existing, shared identically by `list()`/`getById()`; a fix belongs to all three together (`deferred-work.md`, spec-5-1 round 2).
- No Dynamic Type/accessibility-scaling test exists for `EntriesSearchBar`, despite `epic-5-context.md`'s own UX note flagging this as a tight-fit area — pre-existing feature-wide gap, not new to this story.
- The search-skeleton-timer remount fix always restarts a fresh 300ms timer regardless of how long the search was already loading — cosmetic, sub-300ms, narrow remount-while-loading scenario only.
- The source-chip "x" removal fix (keeping the date-range chip's real preset label) has no test for the one scenario it was written for — source and date-range both active, remove the source chip specifically.
- No e2e test exercises `entries-search` with filter params over the real network/Hive pipeline — every I/O-matrix row is still covered at the unit/widget tier, so this is a thin spot in the pyramid's top layer, not a blocking gap.

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean.** No `domain/` file imports `package:flutter`/`data/`. Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`. **AI-feature-through-backend-only policy confirmed respected** — grep for any direct Voyage/Anthropic/Claude API usage across `lib/` returns nothing; `entries-search` is the epic's one AI-backed call, routed through the backend exactly as AGENTS.md requires.
- **A fourth consecutive occurrence of the same systemic shape.** Findings in this retro (1) and in Epics 2's (vault PIN), 3's (entries/chat caches), and 4's (`PendingEntryWriteTracker`) retros are not four unrelated bugs — they are the same missing chokepoint, discovered once per epic because each epic adds its own new piece of per-user state before anyone audits the session-boundary cleanup as a whole. See Action items / Process lessons: this is the point where consolidating into one explicit "wipe all per-account client state" chokepoint (an open question both Epic 3's and Epic 4's retros already raised) stops being a nice-to-have.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope.

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/entries_search_cubit_test.dart test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_search_bar_test.dart` — re-ran: **40/40 passing**.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Epics 1-4's retrospectives (16+10+7+16 = 49 action items, all `status: open`) were all finalized earlier in this same sweep. No dev session has touched the code between any finalization and this retro starting; nothing could plausibly have landed. Recorded as "no evidence of landing," not "not done." No `--set-action-status` proposals from this epic's review.

## Action items

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro):

1. Wire `EntriesSearchCubit.reset()` (cancel the debounce timer, bump `_generation`, clear `_lastQuery`/active filters, emit `ResourceIdle()`) into the same session-boundary chokepoint as Epic 3's and Epic 4's fixes — and, given this is the **fourth** consecutive instance of the identical gap, this retro recommends building that chokepoint as one explicit "wipe all per-account client state" method now, rather than adding a fourth separate point-fix to `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`/`SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`/`AuthCubit.submit()` (finding 1). *Owner: dev.*
2. Give `EntriesSearchBar`'s `TextField` a controller seeded from (and kept in sync with) the cubit's retained query, or have `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState()` force the search `Resource` back to idle unconditionally on every mount, so the search surface never outlives the screen that owns its only visible query-text affordance (finding 2). *Owner: dev.*
3. Bump `_generation` on every keystroke in `onQueryChanged`, not only on clear-to-empty or when a debounce actually fires, so a fast-resolving stale result can never render even momentarily (finding 3). *Owner: dev.*
4. Thread a `CancelToken` through `ApiClient.get()`→`EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()`→`EntriesRepositoryImpl.search()`, cancelling the previous in-flight search at the top of `EntriesSearchCubit._search()` before issuing the next one (finding 4). *Owner: dev — cost/efficiency fix, not a correctness bug.*

Deferred items (tracked, context attached):

5. Finding 5 (`onQueryChanged('')`-after-`close()` untested) — add the one missing close()-adjacent test, mirroring its two siblings.
6. Finding 6 (singleton-identity/query-persistence claim untested) — add a real two-resolution identity test and/or a real navigate-away-and-back round trip asserting the query survives.
7. Finding 7 (combined search+filter race untested through real widget wiring) — add a widget/screen-level test that applies a filter mid-debounce or mid-flight, not only sequentially-settled.
8. `search()`'s DTO→Entity mapping outside try/catch — fix together with `list()`/`getById()`'s identical gap, not in isolation.
9. Dynamic Type/accessibility-scaling test for `EntriesSearchBar` — pre-existing feature-wide gap, revisit with a deliberate accessibility pass (same recurring theme as Epics 1/3/4).
10. Search-skeleton-timer remount fix always restarting a fresh 300ms wait — cosmetic, revisit only if it proves disruptive.
11. Source-chip "x" removal test gap (date-range chip also active) — add the one missing scenario.
12. E2e coverage for combined search+filter over the real network/Hive pipeline — thin-top-of-pyramid gap, not blocking.

Process lessons:

- **This is the fourth consecutive epic to independently discover the same "DI-singleton holding per-user state, never cleared at session boundaries" shape.** Epic 3 proposed the fix for `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository`; Epic 4 proposed the same shape for `PendingEntryWriteTracker` and explicitly asked whether these should be consolidated into one chokepoint rather than fixed one singleton at a time; this epic's evidence is the fourth data point answering that question "yes." The actionable lesson: **before any future epic adds a new DI-singleton that holds any per-user data (search state, draft state, cached preferences, anything keyed to "the current account"), check whether it's wired into whatever session-boundary cleanup chokepoint exists at that time** — this should become a standing item in this project's own story-level review checklist, not something a retrospective keeps re-discovering epic by epic.

## Acceptance verdict

**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria declared — `epics.md` §"Epic 5" gives explicit Given/When/Then per story).

Evidence for "criteria met":
- Semantic search with debounced input, metadata filters, and combined search+filter with non-disruptive clearing all implemented and exercised by a solid test suite — including genuinely correct, genuinely tested retry-safety and generation-guard behavior for the two hardest concurrency questions this epic raised.
- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test` (search/filter scope): 40/40 passing, re-verified directly.
- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, or RNF09 violations found; the AI-feature-through-backend-only policy is confirmed respected with no direct provider calls anywhere in `lib/`.
- No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty).

Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 4 new findings (one — the search cubit's cross-account leakage — is the fourth occurrence of this sweep's recurring severe pattern; the rest are a confirmed UX dead end, a narrow display race, and a cost/efficiency gap), 3 verification gaps, and a backlog of already-known minor items. | 5.2 | `afb4d31` | Metadata filters; story 5.1 round-2 review fixes |
| 5.3 | `9dd6fdf` | Combined search + filter & non-disruptive clearing; story 5.2 round-2 review fixes |

3. Bump `_generation` on every keystroke in `onQueryChanged`, not only on clear-to-empty or when a debounce actually fires, so a fast-resolving stale result can never render even momentarily (finding 3). *Owner: dev.*

# Epic 6 Retrospective — Chat (Send/Receive, Multi-Session, Stream Resilience, Bookmark, Proactive Insight)

Epic 6 is the largest epic in this sweep: 5 stories across 7 commits.

| Story | Commit | Summary |

| 6.1 | `53de1f8` | Send message & receive RAG-grounded streaming response |
| 6.2 | `43351cf` | Multi-session chat history & new conversation; 6.1 round-2 fixes |

| 6.5 | `add1403` | Proactive insight injection & failure isolation |
| — | `09b2496` | RF10 closing snapshot |

**Evidence missing:** no session logs. Epics 1-5's retrospectives (61 action items total) are the previous retros — see Previous-retro follow-through.

## Findings

### New — currently-live findings, most severe first

1. **`ChatCubit` itself — not just its Hive cache — leaks a previous account's full chat content in memory, and the root cause is now identified: there is no production trigger for `sl.reset()` anywhere in the app.** `ChatCubit` is `registerLazySingleton`, living for the app's entire process lifetime; its `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` only runs via `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`/`resetCoreDependencies()`, which grep confirms has **zero production call sites** — used only in test teardown. `ChatCubit.init()`'s own no-op guard (`if (state is ChatReady || isClosed) return`) means the next login's `ChatScreen.initState()` is swallowed silently, so the previous account's `ChatReady.messages` (actual chat content), `.sessions`, `_bookmarkStateByServerId`, and `_scrollOffsets` render as-is to whoever logs in next on the same device. This is strictly broader than Epic 3's Hive-cache finding — even if Epic 3's proposed fix (clear the cache on session-expiry/fresh-login) were implemented, it touches only Hive, never this cubit's in-memory state. *Consequence*: a cross-account content leak of the app's most sensitive data — actual reflective-journaling chat conversations — the fifth occurrence of this exact pattern in five consecutive epics (2, 3, 4, 5, now 6), and the first time the underlying structural cause (the dead `sl.reset()` trigger) has been pinned down directly. — **adversarial lens**
2. **The side drawer's "CONVERSAS" list surfaces the leaked state directly and is independently discoverable.** `AppDrawer`'s `_ConversasSection` reads `ChatReady.sessions` via `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` — the same leaked state from finding 1. *Consequence*: a new user can see a list of a previous account's session titles/timestamps (titles can echo message content) before even opening a conversation, from the drawer alone. — **adversarial lens**
3. **`ChatSessionDto`/`ChatMessageDto` carry no user/account id, so the offline-cache fallback can't filter even if it tried — chat's own instance of the exact pattern Epic 3 found for entries.** The shared Hive boxes get dumped unfiltered on an offline-triggered fallback for whichever account is currently active. — **adversarial lens**
4. **The proactive-insight recency guard (`_insightRequestSeq`) is a single counter shared across every session, not scoped per session.** Triggering an insight on session A (slow to resolve), switching to session B and firing a second trigger there (bumping the shared counter), then switching back to A before request #1 resolves causes A's perfectly valid, non-superseded insight to be silently discarded — the guard's own comment claims it discards only a result superseded by "a later-fired request for the same window," but the counter has no session scoping to make that true. No test exercises this switch-away-then-back-with-an-intervening-other-session-trigger sequence. — **edge-case-hunter**
5. **No client-side timeout ceiling exists if the backend's RAG+LLM pipeline hangs after opening the SSE connection without ever emitting a byte — not even its own documented `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` in-band event.** `receiveTimeout: Duration.zero` deliberately disables dio's own gap timeout, relying entirely on the backend's in-band event as the sole circuit breaker; `ChatCubit._consumeStream` has no `Future.timeout` of its own. *Consequence*: if the backend truly never sends anything, the AI bubble stays `streaming` and the composer stays locked for that session forever, with no client-side recovery short of switching sessions or restarting the app. — **edge-case-hunter**
6. **A message reloaded from history/cache with a persisted `streaming` status — a scenario this codebase's own comments explicitly anticipate — renders as a permanently blinking "zombie" bubble with no way out.** Only `failed`-status bubbles get a retry affordance; `retryMessage()`'s own guard silently no-ops against a `streaming`-status message. *Consequence*: a response abandoned in an earlier session (e.g. by finding 5's own hang, or any other dropped stream) reappears on reload as an indefinitely "typing" bubble the user can neither retry, dismiss, nor distinguish from a genuinely active stream. — **edge-case-hunter**
7. **`generateInsight()` collapses `'generating'`, `'failed'`, `'dismissed'`, and blank-but-non-null `'ready'` content all into the identical `Right(null)`.** `'generating'` is a valid, documented response status (per `openapi.yaml`) and is not a failure — the insight may still be computable server-side — but since no polling/GET endpoint exists for insights and the client's own trigger window has already reset by the time this resolves, a "still generating" result is permanently and silently lost, indistinguishable from a true failure or a genuinely empty result. — **edge-case-hunter**
8. **The proactive-insight message-count trigger fires on attempted sends, not completed ones — and this is exactly the risk `deferred-work.md`'s own spec-6-1 entry predicted, now confirmed materialized in 6.5.** That entry flagged `ChatCubit.sendMessage()`'s internal completer as never awaited by its caller, naming "a future story (6.5's insight-trigger counting is the named candidate)" as the exact risk. `_insightMessagesSinceWindowStart` increments unconditionally the moment `sendMessage()` is called, before the stream's outcome is known — a failed/dropped send counts identically to a successful one toward RF08's "N = 5 user messages" threshold. *Consequence*: a user whose messages keep failing (flaky connectivity that still briefly reports "online") can fire a proactive-insight generation grounded in a conversation that, server-side, may not actually contain those 5 messages. — **edge-case-hunter**; a predicted risk from Epic 6's own earlier story confirmed true by a later story in the same epic.
9. **A self-documented, currently-unresolved defect already exists in shipped code: an aborted connection mid-generation can show "failed" for an answer the backend actually generated successfully, and retry resends as a duplicate question instead of regenerating.** The code's own comment at `api_client.dart` explicitly documents that `receiveTimeout: Duration.zero`'s mitigation "does not fully work" — a connection can still abort mid-generation while the backend persists the answer; the aborted bubble then shows `failed`, and a retry (finding no `serverId`, since even `message_created` never arrived) resends via `sendMessage` as a brand-new message rather than regenerating in place. This is not a newly-discovered bug — it is already acknowledged in the code — but it remains open and user-facing, and connects to the already-known pattern (below) of local client state diverging from backend truth. — **adversarial lens**

### Confirmed clean (explicitly checked, worth recording as a negative result)

- **RF10's architectural boundary is respected exactly as AGENTS.md requires.** `lib/features/chat/**` imports only the abstract `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` port; `EntriesRepository`/anything under `entries/data/` is never imported from chat — grep-confirmed, every textual hit is inside a doc comment explaining the rule, never a live import.
- **The stream re-entrancy guards themselves hold up.** `_isSending`, completer/subscription nulling in both `onDone`/`onError`, and `_cancelInFlightSend` on session switch are each carefully guarded against the specific races their own comments describe; the adversarial lens found no hole in this logic.

### Verification gaps (behavior correct today, unguarded against regression)

10. **The documented `\r\n`-split-across-SSE-chunks fix is untested against an actual split** — no test anywhere in the chat tree uses a `\r` character; every "chunk boundary" test uses plain `\n` splits. (Also independently flagged in `deferred-work.md`'s own spec-6-2 entry — now corroborated by two independent sources.)
11. **Only the `token` SSE event's malformed-payload parsing is tested; the structurally-identical `message_created` and `error` event parsers are not** — the same "guard tested for some methods, not sibling ones" pattern already found in Epics 2, 4, and 5.
12. **`generateInsight()`'s blank-but-non-null content branch (`.trim().isNotEmpty`) is untested** — only the null-content case is covered, so the half of the condition that actually matters per finding 7's own logic isn't proven load-bearing.

### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed)

This epic's reviews produced an unusually large backlog (~30 items across stories 6.1-6.4; story 6.5 produced none of its own). Grouped by theme — all confirmed still present, none newly discovered:

- **Unthrottled-rebuild cluster (4 instances)**: `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` fires on every streamed token; the drawer's "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder`, the drawer's "Novo Chat" disable, and the offline banner all rebuild on every `ChatReady` emission with no `buildWhen`. Harmless today at current message/session volumes; revisit with a throttling pass if streaming performance proves disruptive.
- **Accessibility cluster (5+ instances)**: the streaming bubble has no `Semantics(liveRegion: true)`; the active-session cue is color-only; session switches have no announcement; a bookmark save's outcome has no announcement; several color-only state indicators recur. Consistent with the same recurring theme already noted in Epics 1/3/4/5.
- **"Local state can diverge from backend truth" cluster (2 known instances, now joined by finding 9's self-documented bug)**: `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` can report an error for a bookmark save that actually already succeeded backend-side if the local Hive write fails; a successful `retryMessage()` never persists the regenerated content back to the Hive cache. Same family as finding 9 — a backend success and the client's own record of it can come apart in more than one place in this codebase.
- **Performance / unbounded growth**: `chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` Hive boxes grow forever; `ChatReady.sessions` grows unbounded in memory and renders via a non-virtualized `Column`. Same cluster already flagged for the `entries` Hive box (Epic 4's retro); revisit together at scale.
- **Duplication / minor**: the "most recent session" timestamp comparator is hand-duplicated in three places; the `\r\n` buffer-normalization fix reallocates the whole buffer per chunk (negligible cost); one e2e test's own comment misattributes which mechanism it's actually exercising (documentation accuracy only).
- **Bundled minor/narrow UX items**: bootstrap error screen has no retry button; "Novo Chat" during bootstrap silently no-ops with no feedback; unsent composer draft carries over across a session switch; session timestamps (`HH:mm`, no date) are ambiguous across different days; no loading indicator in the drawer during a session-switch await; `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` reports interface-up, not real reachability (Boundaries explicitly forbid touching this); no test for a flapping connectivity signal; `bookmarkMessage`'s retry path doesn't check `Failure.retryable` (needs a human product decision per the spec's own ambiguous AC, not a mechanical fix); no UI explains why a bookmark failed (scoped out deliberately); a newly bookmarked entry doesn't appear live in an already-open Meus Registros/search screen (consciously accepted trade-off); the bookmark icon's 44pt tap target visually inflates a user bubble's row height versus an AI bubble's (design question, not a defect); `isolatedSideEffect`'s awaited action has no timeout of its own (affects every API call, not specific to chat); a scroll-offset listener can record a transient incorrect value during a session-transition frame (self-corrects).

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean**, including the specifically-verified RF10 boundary (see Confirmed clean above). No `domain/` file imports `package:flutter`/`data/`. Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- **The structural root cause behind this sweep's entire recurring session-boundary theme is now identified, not just pattern-matched.** `resetCoreDependencies()`/`sl.reset()` — the only mechanism that would ever run any DI registration's `dispose:` callback — has no production call site anywhere in `lib/`. Every one of this sweep's five cross-account leakage findings (Epic 2's vault PIN, Epic 3's entries/chat caches, Epic 4's `PendingEntryWriteTracker`, Epic 5's `EntriesSearchCubit`, and this epic's `ChatCubit`) traces back to the same missing production trigger. This is no longer five separate bugs to fix one at a time — it is one missing piece of session-lifecycle plumbing.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope. Findings 1-2 (cross-account content leak) and 5-6 (hung-stream/zombie-bubble) could not be directly observed on a device.

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test test/features/chat` — re-ran: **185/185 passing**.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Epics 1-5's retrospectives (16+10+7+16+12 = 61 action items, all `status: open`) were all finalized earlier in this same sweep. No dev session has touched the code between any finalization and this retro starting; nothing could plausibly have landed. Recorded as "no evidence of landing," not "not done." No `--set-action-status` proposals from this epic's review.

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro):

1. **Build the missing session-lifecycle chokepoint: wire a real production call to `resetCoreDependencies()` (or an equivalent explicit "wipe all per-account client state" method) into the actual session-ending paths** — `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`, `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`'s dead-token branch, `AuthCubit.submit()`'s success path. This is the fifth consecutive epic to independently rediscover a piece of this gap; the open question Epics 3, 4, and 5's retros each raised about consolidating is answered by this epic's evidence: build it now, as the single fix that resolves (or at least gives a real chokepoint for) items 1-3 below and every prior epic's equivalent open item at once. *Owner: dev — highest-priority item in this retro, and arguably in the whole sweep now that the root cause is pinned down.*

10. **The documented `\r\n`-split-across-SSE-chunks fix is untested against an actual split** — no test anywhere in the chat tree uses a `\r` character; every "chunk boundary" test uses plain `\n` splits. (Also independently flagged in `deferred-work.md`'s own spec-6-2 entry — now corroborated by two independent sources.)
11. **Only the `token` SSE event's malformed-payload parsing is tested; the structurally-identical `message_created` and `error` event parsers are not** — the same "guard tested for some methods, not sibling ones" pattern already found in Epics 2, 4, and 5.
12. **`generateInsight()`'s blank-but-non-null content branch (`.trim().isNotEmpty`) is untested** — only the null-content case is covered, so the half of the condition that actually matters per finding 7's own logic isn't proven load-bearing.

### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed)

This epic's reviews produced an unusually large backlog (~30 items across stories 6.1-6.4; story 6.5 produced none of its own). Grouped by theme — all confirmed still present, none newly discovered:

- **Unthrottled-rebuild cluster (4 instances)**: `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` fires on every streamed token; the drawer's "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder`, the drawer's "Novo Chat" disable, and the offline banner all rebuild on every `ChatReady` emission with no `buildWhen`. Harmless today at current message/session volumes; revisit with a throttling pass if streaming performance proves disruptive.
- **Accessibility cluster (5+ instances)**: the streaming bubble has no `Semantics(liveRegion: true)`; the active-session cue is color-only; session switches have no announcement; a bookmark save's outcome has no announcement; several color-only state indicators recur. Consistent with the same recurring theme already noted in Epics 1/3/4/5.
- **"Local state can diverge from backend truth" cluster (2 known instances, now joined by finding 9's self-documented bug)**: `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` can report an error for a bookmark save that actually already succeeded backend-side if the local Hive write fails; a successful `retryMessage()` never persists the regenerated content back to the Hive cache. Same family as finding 9 — a backend success and the client's own record of it can come apart in more than one place in this codebase.
- **Performance / unbounded growth**: `chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` Hive boxes grow forever; `ChatReady.sessions` grows unbounded in memory and renders via a non-virtualized `Column`. Same cluster already flagged for the `entries` Hive box (Epic 4's retro); revisit together at scale.
- **Duplication / minor**: the "most recent session" timestamp comparator is hand-duplicated in three places; the `\r\n` buffer-normalization fix reallocates the whole buffer per chunk (negligible cost); one e2e test's own comment misattributes which mechanism it's actually exercising (documentation accuracy only).
- **Bundled minor/narrow UX items**: bootstrap error screen has no retry button; "Novo Chat" during bootstrap silently no-ops with no feedback; unsent composer draft carries over across a session switch; session timestamps (`HH:mm`, no date) are ambiguous across different days; no loading indicator in the drawer during a session-switch await; `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` reports interface-up, not real reachability (Boundaries explicitly forbid touching this); no test for a flapping connectivity signal; `bookmarkMessage`'s retry path doesn't check `Failure.retryable` (needs a human product decision per the spec's own ambiguous AC, not a mechanical fix); no UI explains why a bookmark failed (scoped out deliberately); a newly bookmarked entry doesn't appear live in an already-open Meus Registros/search screen (consciously accepted trade-off); the bookmark icon's 44pt tap target visually inflates a user bubble's row height versus an AI bubble's (design question, not a defect); `isolatedSideEffect`'s awaited action has no timeout of its own (affects every API call, not specific to chat); a scroll-offset listener can record a transient incorrect value during a session-transition frame (self-corrects).

### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)

- **Architecture / layering — clean**, including the specifically-verified RF10 boundary (see Confirmed clean above). No `domain/` file imports `package:flutter`/`data/`. Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- **The structural root cause behind this sweep's entire recurring session-boundary theme is now identified, not just pattern-matched.** `resetCoreDependencies()`/`sl.reset()` — the only mechanism that would ever run any DI registration's `dispose:` callback — has no production call site anywhere in `lib/`. Every one of this sweep's five cross-account leakage findings (Epic 2's vault PIN, Epic 3's entries/chat caches, Epic 4's `PendingEntryWriteTracker`, Epic 5's `EntriesSearchCubit`, and this epic's `ChatCubit`) traces back to the same missing production trigger. This is no longer five separate bugs to fix one at a time — it is one missing piece of session-lifecycle plumbing.

## Behavior verification

No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope. Findings 1-2 (cross-account content leak) and 5-6 (hung-stream/zombie-bubble) could not be directly observed on a device.

- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
- `fvm flutter test test/features/chat` — re-ran: **185/185 passing**.

## Previous-retro follow-through

Epics 1-5's retrospectives (16+10+7+16+12 = 61 action items, all `status: open`) were all finalized earlier in this same sweep. No dev session has touched the code between any finalization and this retro starting; nothing could plausibly have landed. Recorded as "no evidence of landing," not "not done." No `--set-action-status` proposals from this epic's review.

## Action items

Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro):

1. **Build the missing session-lifecycle chokepoint: wire a real production call to `resetCoreDependencies()` (or an equivalent explicit "wipe all per-account client state" method) into the actual session-ending paths** — `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()`, `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`'s dead-token branch, `AuthCubit.submit()`'s success path. This is the fifth consecutive epic to independently rediscover a piece of this gap; the open question Epics 3, 4, and 5's retros each raised about consolidating is answered by this epic's evidence: build it now, as the single fix that resolves (or at least gives a real chokepoint for) items 1-3 below and every prior epic's equivalent open item at once. *Owner: dev — highest-priority item in this retro, and arguably in the whole sweep now that the root cause is pinned down.*
2. Clear `ChatCubit`'s in-memory state (`messages`, `sessions`, `_bookmarkStateByServerId`, `_scrollOffsets`) at the same chokepoint, since `clearLocalCache()` alone (Hive only) does not reach it (finding 1). *Owner: dev.*
3. Add a user/account id to `ChatSessionDto`/`ChatMessageDto` (or otherwise scope the offline-cache fallback), mirroring whatever fix Epic 3's equivalent entries-side finding lands on (finding 3). *Owner: dev.*
4. Scope `_insightRequestSeq` per session (or otherwise key the recency guard by session id), so switching away and back can't cause a valid insight to be silently dropped (finding 4). *Owner: dev.*
5. Add a client-side timeout ceiling to `ChatCubit._consumeStream`/the SSE consumption path, independent of the backend's own in-band timeout event, so a fully-hung connection can't lock the composer forever (finding 5). *Owner: dev.*
6. Give a reloaded message with persisted `streaming` status either a retry affordance or an automatic transition to a visibly-failed state, so it can't become a permanent zombie bubble (finding 6). *Owner: dev.*
7. Distinguish `generateInsight()`'s `'generating'` status from true failure/empty-result outcomes — at minimum, don't reset the trigger window until the result is actually final (finding 7). *Owner: dev.*
8. Only increment the message-count insight-trigger counter once a send is confirmed to have actually reached the backend (e.g. on `message_created`, not on the bare `sendMessage()` call), closing the gap `deferred-work.md` predicted for this exact story (finding 8). *Owner: dev.*
9. Address the self-documented stream-abort-vs-backend-success defect — e.g. by not marking a bubble `failed` until the backend's own completion signal is confirmed absent, or by surfacing a distinguishable "uncertain outcome" state (finding 9). *Owner: dev — already acknowledged in the code as unresolved; this retro recommends no longer leaving it open.*

Deferred items (tracked, context attached):

10. Finding 10 (`\r\n`-split test gap, independently flagged twice) — add the one test both this review and the original story review already specified.
11. Finding 11 (`message_created`/`error` malformed-payload parsing untested) — add the two missing sibling tests to `token`'s existing one.
12. Finding 12 (`generateInsight()`'s blank-content branch untested) — add the one missing test case.
13. The unthrottled-rebuild cluster (4 instances) — revisit with a `buildWhen`/throttling pass if streaming performance proves disruptive in practice.
14. The accessibility cluster (5+ instances) — revisit with a deliberate accessibility pass across the chat feature, same recurring theme as Epics 1/3/4/5.
15. The "local state can diverge from backend truth" cluster (2 known + finding 9) — revisit together; this family of gaps now has three independent instances across two features.
16. Performance/unbounded-growth cluster (chat Hive boxes, in-memory session list, non-virtualized rendering) — revisit together with Epic 4's equivalent entries-side item, at scale.
17. The bundled minor/narrow UX backlog (bootstrap retry button, draft-carryover, timestamp ambiguity, connectivity-reachability nuance, bookmark retryable-check product decision, bookmark-liveness-in-open-screens, tap-target visual inflation, etc.) — one cleanup pass, not individually urgent.

Process lessons:

- **This epic's own deferred-work.md correctly predicted exactly where a future story would hit an existing gap — and it happened.** Spec-6-1's entry named "6.5's insight-trigger counting" as the specific future risk from the unawaited `sendMessage()` completer, and finding 8 confirms that's exactly what happened. When a deferred item names a specific future story as where a risk will likely surface, that story's own review should explicitly check the named prediction, not just its own new code in isolation — the same lesson Epic 1's retro drew about deferred items naming a future epic as an assumed fix, now seen from the opposite angle (a deferred item naming a future story as where a *risk*, not a fix, will land).
- **The fifth occurrence of the session-boundary-state pattern is the one that finally surfaced its root cause, because this epic's adversarial review specifically went looking for the mechanism (`sl.reset()`'s call sites) rather than re-describing the symptom.** Worth noting for how future reviews approach a recurring finding: after the second or third occurrence of the same shape, it's worth deliberately searching for the shared infrastructure gap underneath, rather than continuing to document each new instance as its own isolated bug.

## Acceptance verdict

**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria declared — `epics.md` §"Epic 6" gives explicit Given/When/Then per story).

Evidence for "criteria met":
- Streaming chat send/receive, multi-session history, dropped-stream resilience, bookmark-to-entry, and proactive insight injection all implemented and exercised by the largest test suite in this sweep (185 tests). The RF10 architectural boundary is correctly respected, verified directly.
- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test` (chat scope): 185/185 passing, re-verified directly.
- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, or RNF09 violations found.
- No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty).

Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 9 new findings (the `ChatCubit` session-boundary leak is the fifth and most revealing instance of this sweep's recurring severe pattern; several others are real, currently-reachable logic bugs in the insight and streaming pipelines), 3 verification gaps, and the largest already-known backlog in this sweep (consistent with this being the largest epic). None represents a failure to deliver this epic's own declared chat functionality, but finding 1's root-cause diagnosis should drive action across every open item from Epics 2 through 6 at once, not be treated as epic-6-scoped alone.

## Open questions

- Now that the root cause (no production `sl.reset()` trigger) is identified, should the fix be "call `resetCoreDependencies()` itself at the session boundary" (simplest, but resets *every* DI singleton, including ones that may not want full disposal) or "build a narrower, purpose-built reset that only touches per-account state" (more work, more precise)? This retro's action item 1 leaves that implementation choice to the dev session.
- Given Epic 7 (export) and Epic 8 (dashboard/account) remain in this sweep and both likely hold their own per-account state, should this fix land *before* those two retros run, so their own reviews aren't spent re-discovering the same root cause a sixth and seventh time? This retrospective sweep can flag the question but can't make the scheduling call itself.

## Assumptions

- **Epic selection:** `-H 6`, continuing the same multi-epic headless sweep. Confirmed via `detect-epic --epic 6`: `story_count: 5`, `pending_stories: []`.
- **No human confirmation was sought** for any step; headless end-to-end. Team discussion (Phase 3) not invoked.
- **Verdict rendered from evidence alone**: **accepted-with-open-items** — criteria met, named findings deferred/tracked, no unfinished stories.
- **The root-cause framing (resetCoreDependencies's missing production call site as the shared cause of five findings across five epics) was synthesized from this sweep's own retro documents and this epic's adversarial-lens evidence, not confirmed with a human.**
